n: Tier 2 HFC-23 calculation from process efficiencies
s: Estimates HFC-23 emissions by multiplying calculated emission factor, HCFC-22 production and the fraction of the year the stream was released untreated.
Tier 2 estimates process CO2 as the carbon entering with feedstocks minus the carbon leaving in primary and secondary products, converted to CO2 by the 44/12 ratio.

loc.section: Figure 3.10 Tier 2 carbon mass balance flow diagram

n: Tier 3 CH4 atmospheric measurement emission calculation (Equation 3.26)
s: Plant CH4 emissions from atmospheric measurement are the time integral of CH4-attributable VOC concentration above background, times wind speed and plume area.

n: Tier 3 CH4 combustion and flare emission factors (Equations 3.28–3.29)
s: CH4 from combustion and flaring uses the same fuel/NCV structure as CO2 with CH4 emission factors in kg/TJ.

n: Tier 3 CH4 emissions from plant-specific data (Equation 3.27)
s: Total CH4 is the sum of combustion, process vent and flare CH4 emissions.

n: Tier 3 CO2 emissions calculation for petrochemical production (Equation 3.20)
s: Total CO2 from petrochemical production is the sum of combustion, process vent and flare emissions.
CO2 from flared waste gas is the sum over gases of flared amount times net calorific value times emission factor.
CO2 from combusted fuel or by-products is the sum over fuels of fuel amount times net calorific value times emission factor.
Total production-related emissions of fluorinated gas k are the sum over plants i and streams j of emitted mass flows f and concentrations C integrated over time t.

n: Tier 3 plant-level summation of HFC-23 emissions
s: National HFC-23 emissions under Tier 3 are the sum of factory-specific emissions across plants and process streams.

n: Tier 3a direct instantaneous HFC-23 emission calculation
s: Calculates instantaneous HFC-23 emissions from a process stream as vent concentration times mass flow times duration.

n: Tier 3b proxy method HFC-23 emission calculation
s: Estimates HFC-23 vent emissions from a standard emission rate per unit of proxy quantity (such as operating rate), adjusted by F, operating-rate ratio, venting duration and recovered quantity.

n: Tier 3b standard emission derivation from plant trials
s: Derives the standard emission per unit of proxy quantity from averaged trial concentration and flow divided by proxy quantity.

n: Tier 3c reactor product monitoring HFC-23 emission calculation
s: Estimates HFC-23 emissions as the time-integrated product of HCFC-22 product mass flow and HFC-23 concentration relative to the product.
CO2 from combustion of bake furnace packing coke is computed from packing coke consumption and baked anode production with sulphur and ash corrections.

n: Carbon content of ferroalloy reducing agent (Equation 4.19)
s: The carbon content of a reducing agent is its fixed carbon fraction plus its volatiles fraction times the carbon content of volatiles.
Tier 1 CH4 emissions from ferroalloy production are the sum over alloy types of production tonnage times a generic emission factor.
Tier 1 ferroalloy CO2 emissions are the sum of product mass times generic emission factor for each ferroalloy type.

n: Ferroalloy Tier 3 CO2 emission equation (reducing agent carbon)
s: Tier 3 ferroalloy CO2 is calculated from reducing agent mass and carbon content, with ore, slag-forming, product and outgoing stream terms in the same equation.

n: Fixed carbon percentage from proximate analysis
s: Fixed carbon percentage is obtained as 100 minus percent ash minus percent volatiles.

loc.section: Tier 3 method: calculations based on amounts and analyses of reducing agents

n: Mass balance basis for Tier 2 and Tier 3 CO2
s: Tier 2 and Tier 3 CO2 calculations assume the carbon content of net anode or paste consumption is ultimately emitted as CO2.

loc.section: Tier 2 or Tier 3 methods for CO_2 emissions

n: Overvoltage coefficient method for PFC emissions (Tier 2 and Tier 3)
s: The overvoltage method estimates CF4 from the overvoltage coefficient, anode effect overvoltage and metal production, with the exact placement of the AEO and CE terms not recoverable from the extracted equation text.

n: PFC emissions Tier 1 method (CF4 and C2F6 by cell technology)
s: Tier 1 estimates aluminium PFC emissions by multiplying default technology-specific emission factors by metal production for each cell technology type.
CO2 from pitch volatiles combustion at anode baking is computed from green anode, hydrogen, baked anode and waste tar quantities.

n: Slag and product carbon mass balance for CO2 (outgoing streams term)
s: CO2 emission from carbon balance is computed from total carbon input minus carbon leaving in product and non-product outgoing streams, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Slope coefficient method for PFC emissions (Tier 2 and Tier 3)
s: The slope method estimates CF4 as the slope coefficient times anode effect minutes per cell-day times metal production, and estimates C2F6 as CF4 times the C2F6/CF4 weight fraction.

n: Tier 1 and Tier 2 SF6 emissions from magnesium casting
s: Tier 1 uses default SF6 factors applied to magnesium production by segment; Tier 2 uses company or national SF6 consumption data as activity data.

n: Tier 1 CH4 emissions from sinter, pig iron and DRI production
s: Tier 1 CH4 for sinter, pig iron and DRI is activity quantity multiplied by a default CH4 emission factor.

n: Tier 1 CO2 emissions from iron and steel production (BOF/EAF/OHF)
s: Non-energy CO2 from steelmaking is computed as the sum of BOF, EAF and OHF crude steel output times their emission factors.

n: Tier 1 CO2 emissions from pig iron, DRI, sinter and pellet production
s: Tier 1 non-energy CO2 for pig iron, DRI, sinter and pellets is activity quantity multiplied by a default emission factor.

n: Tier 1 CO2 emissions from primary magnesium production (Equation 4.28)
s: Tier 1 estimates primary magnesium CO2 emissions from national production from dolomite and magnesite multiplied by default emission factors.

n: Tier 1 CO2 emissions from primary magnesium production (default emission factors)
s: Tier 1 estimates CO2 from primary magnesium production by applying default emission factors to a country's total primary magnesium production.

loc.section: CO_2 EMISSIONS FROM PRIMARY PRODUCTION Tier 1 – default emission factors

s: Tier 1 multiplies national coke production by default emission factors to estimate CO2 and CH4 from coke production.
Lead-production CO2 emissions are estimated by summing direct smelting, Imperial Smelting Furnace and secondary-material emission terms, each multiplied by its emission factor.

n: Tier 1 process CO2 from anode and/or paste consumption (Equation 4.20)
s: Tier 1 total process CO2 is the sum of Prebake and Søderberg metal production multiplied by their technology-specific emission factors.

n: Tier 1 SF6 emissions from magnesium casting (Equation 4.30)
s: Tier 1 estimates SF6 emissions from magnesium casting as total casting or handling mass multiplied by a default SF6 emission factor.

n: Tier 1 zinc production CO2 emission equation (Equation 4.33)
s: Tier 1 estimates CO2 from zinc production by multiplying the quantity of zinc produced by a default emission factor.

n: Tier 1 zinc production CO2 equation by process type (Equation 4.34)
s: When process type is known, Tier 1 sums CO2 from electro-thermic distillation, Imperial Smelting Furnace and Waelz Kiln zinc quantities, each times its process emission factor.

n: Tier 2/3 Prebake CO2 from prebaked anode consumption (Equation 4.21)
s: Prebake CO2 is calculated from metal production and net prebaked anode consumption, corrected for sulphur and ash in baked anodes and converted by the 44/12 mass ratio.

n: Tier 2/3 Søderberg CO2 from paste consumption (Equation 4.24)
s: Søderberg CO2 is calculated from metal production and paste consumption, with corrections for pitch, calcined coke, binder, cyclohexane soluble matter and skimmed dust carbon.

n: Tier 2 CO2 emissions from direct reduced iron production
s: Tier 2 non-energy CO2 from DRI is fuel energy multiplied by fuel carbon content, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Tier 2 CO2 emissions from iron and steel production (carbon mass balance)
s: Tier 2 non-energy CO2 from iron and steel is a carbon mass balance over coke, injected coal, fluxes, electrodes and gas flows, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Tier 2 CO2 emissions from primary magnesium production (Equation 4.29)
s: Tier 2 sums plant-specific primary magnesium production multiplied by plant-specific emission factors and converts the result to Gg.

n: Tier 2 CO2 emissions from sinter production
s: Tier 2 non-energy CO2 from sinter is a carbon mass balance over coke breeze, gases and other process materials, minus sinter off-gas, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Tier 2 country-specific zinc emission factor from EAF dust and coke
s: Tier 2 for Waelz Kiln zinc from EAF dust uses 0.4 t coke per t EAF dust and 1.23 t EAF dust per t zinc when activity data are available.
Tier 2 estimates CO2 from offsite non-integrated coke production using national coking coal, other process materials, and coke and by-product quantities.
Tier 2 estimates CO2 from onsite coke production from coking coal, other process materials, blast furnace gas, and onsite coke and offsite coke oven gas, using carbon contents and a 44/12 factor.

n: Tier 2 SF6 emissions from magnesium casting (Equation 4.31)
s: Tier 2 sets SF6 emissions equal to national or sub-national SF6 consumption in the magnesium industry.
Tier 3 aggregates measured or plant-specific emissions data to national totals, falling back to Tier 2 equations with plant-specific activity data.

n: Basic formula for CO2 emissions from non-energy product uses (Equation 5.1)
s: Estimates CO2 from non-energy product uses as the sum over fuels of non-energy use times carbon content times ODU factor, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Equation 5.4 Tier 1 CO2 from paraffin wax
s: Tier 1 estimates CO2 from paraffin wax as total wax consumption times default carbon content times default ODU factor times 44/12.

n: Equation 5.5 Tier 2 CO2 from paraffin wax by type
s: Tier 2 sums, over wax types i, consumption times carbon content times country-specific ODU factor times 44/12 to estimate CO2 from waxes.
Estimates lubricant CO2 emissions from total lubricant consumption using a single default carbon content and a single default ODU factor.
Estimates lubricant CO2 emissions by summing over lubricant types (motor/industrial oils and greases, excluding 2-stroke use) with type-specific ODU factors.

n: Paraffin wax activity data in energy units
s: Wax consumption must be expressed in energy units (TJ, LHV basis), requiring calorific values to convert physical quantities.
Tier 1 estimates a set of fluorinated compound emissions per product class by multiplying a gas-specific emission factor by capacity utilisation, design capacity and a PV-usage term.

n: Tier 1 heat transfer fluid emission equation (Equation 6.12)
s: Estimates aggregate FC emissions from heat transfer fluids as C6F14 mass using a generic emission factor, capacity utilisation and design capacity.

n: Tier 2 heat transfer fluid mass-balance equation (Equation 6.13)
s: Estimates emissions of a liquid FC from heat transfer fluids via a litre-based mass balance of inventory, purchases, new and retired charge, and recovered amounts, multiplied by density.

n: Tier 2a by-product emission equation for CF4 (Equation 6.8 in Tier 2b form)
s: Estimates CF4 by-product emissions from each gas i as heel-adjusted sum over process types of emission factor times FC consumption times abatement term.
Tier 2a estimates emissions of each FC gas from company-specific gas consumption and emission-control share, using default heel, use-rate and by-product parameters.
Tier 2a process tool emission factors weight the Tier 2b etch and CVD factors by expert-provided gas usage proportions.

n: Tier 2b by-product emission equations (Equations 6.2–6.6, process-type-agnostic form)
s: Estimates CF4, C2F6, CHF3 and C3F8 by-product emissions from a gas i used, using heel fraction, emission factor, FC mass and abatement term, without process-type summation.
Estimates emissions of gas i as the heel-adjusted sum over process types of FC consumption multiplied by non-use and abatement factors.

n: Tier 2b process tool emission factor (simple average)
s: Tier 2b process tool emission factors are the unweighted average of measured data per gas for etch and CVD, rounded to one significant figure.
Good practice for Tier 3 is to document development of company-specific emission factors and explain deviation from generic defaults, optionally aggregating across manufacturers.
Declared annual HFC refrigerant market is production minus exports plus imports plus reclaimed minus destroyed.

n: Annual Sales of new refrigerant (general approach)
s: Annual Sales of new refrigerant is estimated from domestic manufacture, bulk imports and exports, and chemical contained in factory-charged imported or exported equipment.

n: Bank balance for fire protection equipment
s: The bank in year t is the cumulative sum of new agent supplied, imports minus exports minus destruction and prior emissions, minus RRL in year t.

n: Equation 7.1 Net Consumption of a chemical in a specific application
s: Net consumption of a chemical in an application is production plus imports minus exports minus destruction.

n: Equation 7.17 Time dependence of emissions from fire protection equipment
s: Annual fire protection emissions are computed as bank times emission factor plus recovery, release or loss from retired equipment.

n: Equation 7.18 prompt emission sources from other applications
s: Emissions in year t equal current-year sales times the first-year emission factor plus prior-year sales times one minus that factor.

n: Equation 7.19 emissions from other contained applications
s: Contained-application emissions are the sum of manufacturing, product life and disposal emissions, each computed from sales, bank, or disposal with its factor.
Equations 7.2A and 7.2B are titled for emissions from a specific application and from an application with banks, but their formula content is not in this batch.

n: Equation 7.2A Emissions of a chemical from a specific application (prompt emissions)
s: Annual emissions for applications without banks equal net consumption multiplied by a composite emission factor.

n: Equation 7.2B Emissions of a chemical from an application with banks
s: Annual emissions with banks equal net consumption times a first-year composite emission factor plus total banked chemical times a bank composite emission factor.

n: Equation 7.3 General mass balance equation for Tier 1b
s: Emissions equal annual sales of new chemical minus the net change in charge of equipment stock.

n: Equation 7.5 Emission estimation method for solvent uses
s: Estimates HFC/PFC solvent emissions in year t from current and previous-year sales, an emission factor and solvents destroyed in year t-1.

n: Equation 7.6 Emission estimation method for aerosol uses
s: Estimates HFC/PFC aerosol emissions in year t from aerosol products sold in years t and t-1 and a first-year emission factor.

n: Equation index for Chapter 7 (ODS substitutes emission equations)
s: Chapter 7 lists emission equations 7.1 to 7.19 covering net consumption, mass balance, lifecycle phases, solvents, aerosols, foams, refrigeration and fire protection, but the formulas themselves are not in this batch.

n: General emission-factor approach for closed-cell foams (Equation 7.7)
s: Estimates HFC emissions from closed-cell foam in year t from first-year losses, annual losses from the bank, decommissioning losses, and minus emissions prevented by recovery and destruction.

n: Generic calculation method for emissions from open-celled foams (Equation 7.8)
s: Sets open-celled foam emissions in year t equal to total HFC used in manufacturing new open-cell foam in that year.
Equation 7.15 estimates annual HFC refrigerant needs as a QC comparison against declared refrigerant market.
The MAC bank in a year is the sum of refrigerant charged into new MACs over the assumed average lifetime back to the current year.
Container emissions for MACs equal cylinder and small-can refrigerant sold multiplied by their respective container heel fractions.

loc.section: Calculation of Different Types of Emissions

s: End-of-life emissions for MACs equal the charge of MACs disposed times the residual charge fraction times (1 minus recovery efficiency).

n: MAC worked example (Tier 2a, Box 7.4) – parameter values and totals
s: The Box 7.4 hypothetical MAC example uses stated assumptions (m=0.7 kg, k=0, d=12, x=26%, n_rec=0) and yields total emissions 0.02·RM_cy + 0.2·RM_sc + 0.182·ΣN + 0.518·N_1994 kg, but the text says assumptions are for example only.
Bank dynamics are computed as a year-by-year sequential calculation of non-emitted consumption (consumption minus emissions).

n: Original Total Charge of Retiring Equipment
s: Original total charge of retiring equipment is estimated like total charge of new equipment but using quantities from the year of manufacture or import of the retiring equipment.

loc.section: Total Charge of New Equipment = Chemical to Charge Domestically Manufactured Equipment that is not Factory-Charged + Chemical to Charge Domestically Manufactured Equipment that is Factory-Charged + Chemical to Charge Imported Equipment that is not Factory-Charged + Chemical Contained in Factory-Charged Imported Equipment – Chemical Contained in Factory-Charged Exported Equipment

n: Other applications method choice: emissive versus contained split
s: Other applications are split into emissive and contained classes by survey, and Approach A (emission-factor) methods are recommended.

n: RAC Tier 1a/b back-calculation of refrigerant banks
s: The RAC Tier 1a/b method back-calculates refrigerant banks from the reporting year to the year of introduction using sales and growth inputs.

n: Refrigerant charge emissions of new equipment
s: Charging emissions equal the HFC amount charged into new equipment multiplied by an assembly-loss emission factor k.
Container-management emissions equal the HFC market for new equipment and servicing multiplied by a container emission factor c.
End-of-life emissions equal the HFC initially charged into systems installed d years earlier, multiplied by residual charge fraction and by one minus recovery efficiency.
Operation and servicing emissions equal the HFC banked in existing systems multiplied by the annual bank emission rate x.

n: Summary emissions equation based on lifecycle phases
s: Total emissions of each PFC or HFC are the sum of assembly/manufacturing, operation and disposal emissions.
Tier 1a/b estimates emissions from consumption and a composite emission factor; the example uses a default of 15 percent of the bank annually.

n: Tier 1a default emission factors for HFC foam sub-applications
s: IPCC default factors for HFC foam sub-applications give product life in years, first-year loss %, annual loss % and maximum potential end-of-life loss % for each sub-application.

n: Tier 1a Gamlen-model bank method for closed-cell foam
s: A Tier 1a method based on the Gamlen model estimates foam emissions from the total closed-cell foam bank of a country using consumption by year and a year of introduction.

loc.section: Using the Tier 1a method based on Gamlen model

s: Tier 2 estimates HFC/PFC emissions from ODS substitutes by calculating net consumption at sub-application level and applying either emission factors (Tier 2a) or a mass-balance approach (Tier 2b).

loc.section: TIER 2 METHODS – APPLIED AT THE SUB-APPLICATION LEVEL

s: Refrigerant emissions for each of six sub-applications are summed from container, charging, lifetime and end-of-life components, each computed from factors and quantities in kg.

n: Tier 2b mass-balance emission estimation for refrigerants
s: Refrigerant emissions are estimated by a mass balance of annual new refrigerant sales, new equipment charge, retiring equipment charge and intentional destruction.

n: Total Charge of New Equipment (general approach)
s: Total charge of new equipment is estimated from chemical used to charge domestic and imported equipment, adjusted for factory-charged exports and imports.

loc.section: Total Charge of New Equipment = Chemical to Charge Domestically Manufactured Equipment that is not Factory-Charged + Chemical to Charge Domestically Manufactured Equipment that is Factory-Charged + Chemical to Charge Imported Equipment that is not Factory-Charged + Chemical Contained in Factory-Charged Imported Equipment – Chemical Contained in Factory-Charged Exported Equipment

n: AWACS用户质量平衡法排放量 (Equation 8.13)
s: Computes SF6 emissions from AWACS aircraft by a user-level mass balance of inventory change, acquisitions, disbursements and fleet charge change.
Estimates SF6 emissions from AWACS aircraft as a fixed per-plane emission factor times the number of planes in the fleet.

n: Emissions from SF6 recycling and destruction (Equations 8.8 and 8.9)
s: Estimates recycling and destruction emissions as emission factor times quantity of SF6 fed into each process, excluding recycling at chemical production facilities.

n: 粘性/弹性应用延迟排放计算 (Equation 8.19)
s: Assigns emissions of adiabatic-property applications with a three-year delay from sales.

n: Equipment disposal and final use emissions - pure mass-balance (Equation 8.7A)
s: Estimates disposal and final use emissions from nameplate capacity of retired equipment minus SF6 recovered from it.

n: Equipment disposal emissions from sealed-pressure equipment - hybrid term (Equation 8.7B)
s: Gives the hybrid disposal formula where sealed-pressure disposal emissions are estimated with an emission-factor-based term.
Adds emission-factor-based installation emissions for low-emission equipment to the mass-balance installation term.
Estimates installation emissions as SF6 used to fill equipment minus nameplate capacity of new equipment.
Combines mass-balance emissions for high-rate processes with emission-factor emissions for low-rate processes at a manufacturer.
Estimates SF6 emissions from an equipment manufacturer from changes in inventory, acquisitions and disbursements of SF6.
Adds emission-factor-based use emissions for equipment not covered by the mass-balance term.
Estimates use emissions from SF6 recharged at servicing minus SF6 recovered at servicing.

n: N2O emissions from other product uses (Equation 8.24)
s: Estimates annual N2O emissions from product uses as the sum over application types of the average of current and prior-year supplied quantities multiplied by an emission factor.

n: 瞬时排放 (Prompt emissions) 计算 (Equation 8.23)
s: Estimates prompt SF6 and PFC emissions in a year from sales in the current and previous year.
Estimates retiring nameplate capacity from new nameplate capacity, a growth rate g and equipment lifetime L when direct data are unavailable.

n: SF6 emissions from manufacturing of electrical components (cast resin and bushings)
s: Estimates SF6 emissions from components with 1 percent or less SF6 by weight by applying the pure mass-balance manufacturing formula with SF6 contained in new equipment set to zero.

loc.section: SF_6 EMISSIONS FROM MANUFACTURING OF ELECTRICAL COMPONENTS

n: 双层玻璃窗 SF6 排放计算 (Equations 8.20–8.22)
s: Computes SF6 emissions from double-glazed sound-proof windows across assembly, annual leakage and disposal stages.

n: SF6 mass-balance and emission-factor Tier 3 hybrid approach (Germany, HV and MV)
s: Annex 8A illustrates a Tier 3 hybrid approach combining mass-balance (MB) equations for some SF6 life-cycle stages with emission factors (EF) for others, with separate HV and MV legends.

loc.section: Annex 8A Examples of Tier 3 national SF_6 inventory systems

s: Tier 1 estimates SF6/PFC emissions from electrical equipment by multiplying default emission factors by consumption or nameplate capacity at each life-cycle stage.

n: 大学与研究粒子加速器 Tier 1 国家级排放计算 (Equation 8.14)
s: Estimates national SF6 emissions from university and research particle accelerators by multiplying accelerator count by use factor, charge factor and emission factor.

n: 工业与医用粒子加速器 Tier 1 国家级排放计算 (Equation 8.18)
s: Estimates national SF6 emissions from industrial and medical accelerators by count of SF6-using accelerators, process-specific charge factor and emission factor.
Tier 1 stage formulas multiply stage-specific emission factors by manufacturer consumption or nameplate capacity, with disposal using fraction of SF6 remaining at retirement.

n: Tier 2 emission factor development from life-cycle-stage emissions
s: Derives emission factors by dividing life-cycle-stage emissions from surveyed manufacturers and utilities by the matching SF6 consumption or equipment capacity, with downstream recycling and destruction emissions added separately.

n: 大学与研究粒子加速器 Tier 2 加速器级排放因子法 (Equation 8.15)
s: Multiplies a 7 percent default emission factor by the sum of individual accelerator SF6 charges when charge data are available.
Tier 2 disposal emissions subtract recovered and recycled, reused or destroyed SF6 from the SF6 remaining at retirement.

n: 大学与研究粒子加速器 Tier 3 加速器级质量平衡法 (Equations 8.16–8.17)
s: Computes each accelerator's SF6 emissions by mass balance and sums them to the total emissions.
Tier 3 national total is the sum over facilities of manufacturing, installation, use, disposal and recycling/destruction emissions.
Simplified Tier 3 user-emission formula reformulated in facility-level gas flows for countries meeting pure mass-balance criteria.

n: Acrylonitrile CO2 and CH4 worksheet calculation
s: The worksheets compute CO2 and CH4 emissions from acrylonitrile production as production times emission factor, with unit conversion to Gg.
The 2B3 worksheet multiplies adipic acid production by an N2O emission factor and converts kg to Gg.
The 2B1 worksheet computes CO2 from ammonia fuel use via fuel carbon content and oxidation factor, then subtracts CO2 recovered for urea production.

n: By-product and fugitive fluorinated compound emission worksheets
s: The worksheets compute by-product and fugitive fluorinated compound emissions as principal compound production times an emission factor, with the fugitive sheet describing a Tier 1 default factor.

n: Caprolactam, Glyoxal and Glyoxylic Acid N2O worksheet (2B4)
s: The 2B4 worksheet computes N2O emissions per chemical as production times an emission factor, converted to Gg.

n: Carbide acetylene use and total CO2 worksheets (2B5, sheets 3 of 6 and 4 of 6)
s: The 2B5 worksheets compute CO2 from calcium carbide used in acetylene production and sum silicon carbide, calcium carbide and acetylene CO2 into a total.

n: Carbide CH4 worksheets (2B5, sheets 5 of 6 and 6 of 6)
s: The 2B5 worksheets compute CH4 from silicon carbide production using either raw material consumption or carbide produced; only one should be used.

n: Carbide Production CO2 worksheet (2B5, sheets 1 of 6 and 2 of 6)
s: The 2B5 worksheets compute CO2 from petroleum coke consumption or from carbide produced; the compiler should use one of these two sheets, not both.

n: Carbon black CO2 and CH4 worksheet calculation
s: The worksheets compute CO2 and CH4 emissions from carbon black production as production times emission factor, with unit conversion to Gg.

n: Cement Production CO2 worksheet (2A1, sheet 1 of 2) clinker mass
s: The 2A1 worksheet computes clinker mass in each cement type as the product of cement mass and clinker fraction.

n: Cement Production CO2 worksheet (2A1, sheet 2 of 2) clinker-based CO2
s: The 2A1 worksheet derives clinker produced in the country from clinker mass adjusted for trade, then multiplies by a clinker emission factor to obtain CO2.

n: EDC/VCM production CH4 emission worksheet calculation
s: The worksheet computes CH4 emissions from ethylene dichloride or vinyl chloride monomer production as activity times emission factor, converted to Gg.

n: Emissions of SF6 and PFCs from other prompt emissive applications (2G2)
s: Emissions from other prompt emissive applications in year t equal the average of sales in year t and year t-1, expressed in Gg by dividing by 10^3.

n: Ethylene oxide CO2 and CH4 worksheet calculation
s: The worksheets compute CO2 and CH4 emissions from ethylene oxide production as production amount times emission factor, with unit conversion to Gg.

n: Ferroalloy, aluminium, lead, zinc and magnesium emission worksheets
s: The worksheets compute metal-industry CO2, CH4, CF4, C2F6 and SF6 emissions as production or casting amount times emission factor, with unit conversion to Gg.
The 2A3 worksheet computes glass CO2 emissions from total glass production, an emission factor, and the average annual cullet ratio.

n: HFC-23 emissions from HCFC-22 production worksheet calculation
s: The worksheet computes HFC-23 emissions as HCFC-22 produced in kg times an emission factor, converted to Gg.
Emissions from aerosol products equal sold-in-year quantity times emission factor plus prior-year quantity times one minus emission factor, with conversion to Gg by dividing by 10^3.

n: HFC/PFC bank emission formula for refrigeration and air conditioning (2F1)
s: Emissions in the inventory year from refrigeration and air conditioning equal the bank times average emission factor divided by 100 plus agent in retired equipment.
Fire protection emissions in the inventory year equal bank times average emission factor divided by 100 plus retired agent times (1 minus recovery rate divided by 100).
Foam blowing agent emissions in the inventory year equal original charge times annual loss factor divided by 100 plus first-year loss.
Emissions from other HFC/PFC applications equal sold-in-year quantity times emission factor plus prior-year quantity times one minus emission factor, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^3.
Solvent emissions equal sold-in-year quantity times emission factor plus prior-year quantity times one minus emission factor, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^3.

n: Iron and steel CO2 and CH4 worksheet calculation
s: The worksheets compute CO2 and CH4 emissions from iron and steel production as production times emission factor, with unit conversion to Gg.
The 2A2 worksheet multiplies lime mass by an emission factor to obtain CO2 emissions and converts tonnes to Gg.

n: N2O emission formula from product uses (2G3)
s: N2O emissions from product uses equal the average of year t and year t-1 supply multiplied by the emission factor, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^3.
The 2B2 worksheet multiplies nitric acid production by an N2O emission factor and converts kg to Gg.

n: Non-energy product lubricant and paraffin wax CO2 worksheet calculation
s: The worksheets compute CO2 emissions from lubricant and paraffin wax use from energy consumed, carbon content, oxidation fraction and the 44/12 CO2/C conversion.

n: Other Process Uses of Carbonates CO2 worksheet (2A4) with Tier 1 carbonate defaults
s: The 2A4 worksheet multiplies carbonate mass consumed by an emission factor for each use type, with Tier 1 default carbonate composition rules in the footnotes.

n: Petrochemical EDC/VCM CO2 worksheet (2B8, sheet 5 of 12)
s: The 2B8 EDC/VCM worksheet multiplies EDC or VCM produced by an emission factor to obtain CO2.

n: Petrochemical ethylene worksheets with geographic adjustment (2B8, sheets 3 of 12 and 4 of 12)
s: The 2B8 ethylene CO2 worksheet applies a geographic adjustment factor in percent, while the CH4 worksheet is computed without it.

n: Petrochemical methanol worksheets (2B8, sheets 1 of 12 and 2 of 12)
s: The 2B8 methanol worksheets multiply methanol produced by CO2 or CH4 emission factors, with process and feedstock types to be specified by the compiler.

n: Semiconductor fluorinated compound Tier 1 emission worksheet
s: The worksheet estimates Tier 1 fluorinated compound emissions from capacity utilization, design capacity, a default emission factor per m2 of silicon processed, and a CO2-equivalent conversion factor.

n: SF6 electrical equipment manufacturing, installation, use, disposal and total emission formulas (2G1)
s: The 2G1 worksheets compute SF6 emissions from electrical equipment by stage as C = A * B, F = D * E, I = G * H, L = J * K, total M = C + F + I + L, and N = M/10^3.
Adiabatic-use SF6 emissions in year t equal sales into application in year t-3, expressed in Gg by dividing by 10^3.

n: SF6 emissions from AWACS military applications (2G2)
s: SF6 emissions from AWACS aircraft equal the national fleet count times the emission factor per plane, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^6.

n: SF6 emissions from industrial and medical particle accelerators (2G2)
s: SF6 emissions from industrial and medical particle accelerators equal count times charge factor times emission factor, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^6.
Sound-proof glazing SF6 emissions combine assembly emissions as A*B and leakage emissions as D*E, with disposal emissions as G*(1 – H) and total emissions summed.

n: SF6 emissions from university and research particle accelerators (2G2)
s: SF6 emissions from research particle accelerators equal count times use factor times charge factor times emission factor, converted to Gg by dividing by 10^6.

n: Soda Ash Production CO2 worksheets (2B7, natural soda ash)

s: Calculates annual change in dead wood and litter stocks for each cohort in transition by adding the net change rate to the previous year's stock, then converting to carbon and multiplying by cohort area.

n: Default tree cover simplified estimate of annual carbon accumulation
s: Estimates annual tree carbon accumulation by multiplying default percent tree cover by settlement area and default growth rates from Table 8.1.
Estimates DOM carbon change per category from net change in dead wood and litter (inputs minus outputs) times carbon fraction times area.
Estimates annual DOM carbon change from the difference between DOM stocks at two inventory times divided by the interval, times carbon fraction and area.

n: Equation 8.1 annual carbon change in live biomass pools in Settlements Remaining Settlements
s: Biomass carbon change in Settlements Remaining Settlements is the sum of tree, shrub and herbaceous increment terms.

n: Equation 8.2 crown cover area based biomass increment (Tier 2a)
s: Annual biomass carbon increment equals the sum over classes and woody perennial types of crown cover area times the crown cover area-based growth rate.

n: Equation 8.3 individual woody plant growth method (Tier 2b)
s: Annual live biomass carbon increment equals the sum over classes and perennial types of number of individuals times annual average carbon accumulation per individual.
Estimates the net change rate of dead wood and litter as average annual inputs minus average annual losses, computed separately for each pool.

n: Soil organic carbon stock change Tier 2 with stock change factors
s: Tier 2 mineral soil estimate uses country-specific reference C stocks and stock change factors F_LU, F_MG and F_I within Equation 2.25.

Estimates net change in dead wood and litter stocks as the difference between final and initial average stocks divided by the number of years between inventories, with negative values indicating loss.

n: Tier 1 biomass assumption for Settlements Remaining Settlements
s: Tier 1 assumes no change in live biomass carbon stocks, so growth and loss terms balance.

n: Tier 1 biomass change on land converted to Settlements (Equation 2.16 usage)
s: For Tier 1, biomass change on land converted to settlements is estimated by applying Equation 2.16 with B_After set to zero and then multiplying the summed result by 44/12 to obtain CO2.

n: Tier 1 dead organic matter change on land converted to Settlements
s: At Tier 1, all dead wood and litter carbon on converted land is assumed lost, with stocks after conversion set to zero, and the net change is computed per hectare, converted to carbon, and multiplied by area converted.

n: Tier 1 soil organic carbon change for mineral soils converted to Settlements
s: Annual soil organic carbon emissions or removals are the difference in stocks over time divided by the time dependence D of the stock change factors, with a default D of 20 years.

n: Tier 2 Method A crown cover area method
s: Estimates biomass carbon change in settlements remaining settlements from total crown cover area per perennial type using Equation 8.2 and CRW rates.

n: Tier 2 Method B individual plant growth method
s: Estimates annual carbon sequestration by multiplying plant counts per class by carbon increment per plant using Equation 8.3.

n: Tier 2 step-by-step method for dead organic matter on land converted to Settlements
s: Tier 2 DOM change on converted land uses representative areas by conversion stage and stock changes per hectare, with carbon conversion by carbon fraction and multiplication by area.

n: Tier 2a/2b root:shoot ratio and Tier 1 loss-balance context for DOM and soil pools
s: The chapter estimates DOM and soil carbon changes in Settlements Remaining Settlements, but the excerpt does not give the formulas for these pools.

n: Biomass carbon change on Land Converted to Other Land (basic method)
s: Change in biomass carbon on land converted to Other Land is estimated from carbon before conversion minus carbon after conversion, with B_AFTER set to zero by default.

n: Default uncertainty for Tier 1 Land Converted to Other Land
s: In the absence of other estimates, a default uncertainty of +75% of the estimated mean CO2 emission may be assumed at Tier 1.

n: Mineral soil organic carbon change, Tier 1 (Equation 2.25)
s: Annual soil carbon emissions or removals are estimated from the difference in stocks between initial and last year divided by the stock-change time dependence D, with a default of 20 years.

n: Activity data choice for manure CH4 (animal population and MMS usage)
s: Manure CH4 estimation requires animal population data by climatic zone and manure management system usage data by species.
Annual average livestock population is estimated as days alive multiplied by number of animals produced annually, divided by 365.

n: Annual N excretion rate from default N excretion rate and typical animal mass (Equation 10.30)
s: Annual N excretion per head is obtained by multiplying the daily N excretion rate per 1000 kg animal mass by the typical animal mass and by 365 days.
Annual nitrogen excretion per animal of livestock category T is defined in terms of a default excretion rate and a typical animal mass.

n: Approximate emission factor by weight scaling
s: For uncharacterised livestock, an approximate emission factor is scaled from a similar digestive-system species by weight raised to the 0.75 power, usable only for significance screening.

loc.section: 10.2.4 Characterisation for livestock without species: Specific emission estimation methods

s: Daily N intake for cattle is derived from gross energy intake and dietary crude protein percent using constants 18.45 and 6.25; the layout is partly garbled in the source.
Daily N retained by cattle is defined from milk production, milk protein percent, weight gain and net energy for growth, with NRC-derived constants; the equation layout is garbled in the source.

n: CH_4 emission factor from manure management (Equation 10.23, Tier 2)
s: Tier 2 emission factor for a livestock category is built from daily volatile solids, maximum methane producing capacity B_o, system MCF values and a fraction of manure per system.
Annual CH4 from manure management is the sum over livestock categories of emission factor times head count, with the stated unit Gg CH4 per year.
The source states that regional emission factors for dairy cows are calculated based on equation 10.23, but the equation itself is not reproduced in this batch.

loc.section: Annex 10A.2 Data underlying methane default emission factors for Manure Management

n: Direct N2O emissions from manure management (Equation 10.25)
s: Direct N2O emissions from manure management are computed by summing, over livestock categories and manure management systems, the product of head count, annual N excretion per head, the fraction managed in each system, and the system emission factor, then converting N2O-N to N2O by 44/28.

n: Direct N2O emissions from manure management systems (Step 2)
s: Direct N2O per MMS is the MMS emission factor multiplied by the nitrogen managed in that system, reported in kg N2O.

n: Dry matter intake conversion from GE with default energy density
s: Dry matter intake is obtained by dividing GE by feed energy density, with 18.45 MJ per kg dry matter as default when feed-specific data are unavailable.
Enteric methane is estimated by characterising population subgroups, estimating kg CH4 per animal per year, and multiplying by subgroup populations then summing.

n: Four-step manure management CH4 estimation procedure
s: Manure CH4 is estimated by collecting population data, assigning emission factors per subcategory, summing by species, then summing across species.

n: Gross energy requirement for cattle, buffalo and sheep (Equation 10.16)
s: GE requirement is derived from summed net energy components (maintenance, activity, lactation, work, pregnancy, growth, wool) divided by REM and REG terms, with only terms relevant to each category used.

n: Indirect N2O emissions from manure management (volatilisation, Step 3)
s: Volatilised N is the MMS volatilisation fraction times NE_MMS, and indirect N2O is that volatilised N times EF_4.

n: Indirect N2O from leaching and runoff from manure management (Equation 10.29)
s: Indirect N2O from leached and runoff manure N is estimated by multiplying leached N by EF5 and converting N to N2O with 44/28.

n: Indirect N2O from volatilisation of N from manure management (Equation 10.27)
s: Indirect N2O from manure N volatilised as NH3 and NOx is estimated by multiplying the volatilised N by EF4 and converting N to N2O with 44/28.

n: Managed manure N available for application to soils, feed, fuel or construction (Equation 10.34)
s: Managed manure N available is defined over livestock categories and management systems from population, excretion, system share and loss fraction, plus bedding N; the equation layout is garbled.

n: Manure N available for soils, feed, fuel or construction (Step 4)
s: Managed manure N available for use is calculated per MMS using total N loss fraction and bedding N, then summed over all MMS.

n: N losses due to leaching and runoff from manure management systems (Equation 10.28)
s: Nitrogen lost by leaching and runoff from manure management systems is estimated by multiplying excreted N per category and system by the leaching/runoff percentage and summing; it should only be used where country-specific leaching/runoff fractions exist.

n: N losses due to volatilisation from manure management (Equation 10.26)
s: Nitrogen lost as NH3 and NOx by volatilisation from manure management is estimated by multiplying excreted N per category and system by the system volatilisation percentage and summing.

n: N2O direct emission from manure management (MMS N excretion step)
s: The worksheet procedure computes manure N per MMS by multiplying head count, N excretion rate per head and MMS fraction.
Net energy for pregnancy equals the pregnancy coefficient times daily maintenance net energy, with the coefficient taken from Table 10.7.

n: NE_wool (net energy to produce wool, sheep)
s: Net energy for wool production equals the energy value of wool times annual wool production per sheep.

n: NE_work (net energy for work, cattle and buffalo)
s: Net energy for draft work is estimated as 0.10 times daily maintenance net energy times hours of work per day.

n: Net energy for activity (NE_a) for cattle and buffalo
s: Net energy for activity for cattle and buffalo equals the activity coefficient C_a times NE_m.

n: Net energy for activity (NE_a) for sheep
s: Net energy for activity for sheep equals the feeding-situation coefficient C_a times live weight.

n: Net energy for growth (NE_g) for cattle and buffalo
s: Net energy for growth for cattle and buffalo is given by a printed equation with a leading constant 22.02, average live body weight, weight gain and a sex coefficient C with mature weight MW; the denominator grouping is not confirmed in the extracted text.

n: Net energy for growth (NE_g) for sheep
s: Net energy for growth for sheep uses weight gain from weaning to one year with empirical constants a and b that vary by sheep category; the leading expression is not confirmed in the extracted text.

n: Net energy for lactation (NE_l) for cattle and buffalo
s: Net energy for lactation for cattle and buffalo is a function of daily milk production and milk fat content.

n: Net energy for lactation (NE_l) for sheep, milk production known
s: For sheep with known milk production, net energy for lactation is milk production times the net energy value of milk.
Net energy for maintenance is the category coefficient Cf_i multiplied by live weight raised to the 0.75 power.
When sheep birth-type data are missing, C_pregnancy is computed from double and single birth fractions if lambs per pregnant ewe is between 1 and 2.

n: Tier 1 enteric fermentation CH4 inventory method
s: Tier 1 estimates enteric CH4 by multiplying default emission factors by animal population counts and summing across categories, requiring only readily available population data.
Tier 2 annual N excretion equals daily N intake times one minus retention fraction times 365 days.

n: Tier 2 emission factor equation for enteric fermentation
s: Tier 2 derives an annual enteric CH4 emission factor per livestock category from gross energy intake and the methane conversion factor Ym.

n: Tier 2 manure management CH4 emission factor (EF(T))
s: Computes annual CH4 emission factor for livestock category T from annual VS production, maximum methane capacity B0 and weighted MCF and MS fractions.
Estimates daily VS excretion from gross energy intake, digestibility, urinary energy fraction and ash content.

n: Animal manure N applied to soils (F_AM)
s: Manure N applied to soils is manure N available minus fractions used for feed, fuel and construction, or N_MMS_Avb unadjusted if those data are unavailable.

n: Direct N2O emissions from managed soils (Tier 1), Equation 11.1
s: Tier 1 estimates annual direct N2O-N from managed soils as the sum of N-input emissions, organic soil emissions and urine/dung emissions from grazing animals.

n: Direct N2O emissions from managed soils (Tier 2), Equation 11.2
s: Tier 2 expands the N-input term by disaggregating synthetic and organic N emission factors across n conditions i, while retaining the common crop residue/SOM term, organic soil and urine/dung terms.

n: Dry-weight correction of reported crop yields
s: Dry matter crop yield is obtained by multiplying fresh yield by the dry matter fraction of the harvested crop.

n: Equation 11.12 Annual CO2 emissions from lime application
s: Estimates annual CO2-C emissions from carbonate lime applied to soils as the sum of limestone and dolomite amounts times their emission factors.

n: N deposited by grazing animals on pasture, range and paddock (F_PRP)
s: Urine and dung N deposited by grazing animals is the sum over livestock categories of head count times N excretion times the fraction deposited on pasture.

n: N from crop residues and forage/pasture renewal (F_CR)
s: Crop residue N returned to soils is summed over crop types from harvested area, dry matter yield, residue ratios, N contents and removal fractions, including below-ground residues.

n: N from organic N additions applied to soils (F_ON)
s: Annual organic N applied to soils other than by grazing animals is the sum of manure, sewage, compost and other organic amendment N.

n: N mineralised from soil organic C loss in mineral soils (F_SOM)
s: Net N mineralised from mineral soil carbon loss is calculated from average annual soil carbon loss and the soil C:N ratio R.

n: N2O direct and indirect completeness check for managed land
s: Complete coverage of direct and indirect N2O from managed land requires estimating all anthropogenic input and activity sub-categories where they occur.

n: N2O from atmospheric deposition of volatilised N (Equation 11.9, Tier 1)
s: Tier 1 equation estimating annual N2O-N from atmospheric deposition of N volatilised from managed soils, using synthetic fertiliser, organic N and grazing urine/dung inputs with volatilisation fractions and EF4.

n: N2O from atmospheric deposition of volatilised N (Equation 11.11, Tier 2 disaggregated form)
s: Tier 2 expansion of Equation 11.9 that disaggregates synthetic fertiliser N by conditions i with condition-specific Frac_GASF_i.
Tier 1 equation estimating annual N2O-N from leaching and runoff of N additions in regions where leaching/runoff occurs.

Direct N2O-N from drained or managed organic soils is calculated from managed organic soil area multiplied by EF_2 for cropland/grassland and forest land, split by temperate/tropical and nutrient-rich/nutrient-poor climate and nutrient classes.

n: N2O-N from N inputs to managed soils (Tier 1)
s: The Tier 1 N-input term multiplies the sum of synthetic fertiliser, organic N, crop residue and SOM-mineralised N by EF_1 (with EF_1FR for flooded rice).

n: N2O-N from urine and dung on grazed soils (Tier 1)
s: Direct N2O-N from urine and dung on pasture is the sum of F_PRP times EF_3PRP for cattle/poultry/pigs and for sheep/other animals.

n: Tier 1/2 direct N2O emission estimation from managed soils
s: Direct N2O emissions from managed soils are estimated with Tier 1 or Tier 2 equations using emission factors EF1, EF2 and EF3PRP, with Tier 2 allowing country-specific factors.

n: Tier 2 and Tier 3 liming QA/QC and time series consistency
s: Good practice requires internal and independent QA/QC of liming data and results, and consistent methods across the time series.

n: Urea activity data estimation from production and trade (Tier 1)
s: Annual urea applied to soils can be approximated from domestic production plus imports minus exports, optionally refined with sales or usage data.
Annual CO2-C emissions from urea application are estimated as the product of annual urea amount and an emission factor.
The AFA HWP contribution to AFOLU net CO2 emissions is computed from HWP carbon stock changes and cross-border transfers, or equivalently from harvest and HWP carbon release.

n: Equation 12.2 HWP products placed in use from domestic consumption

n: Equation 12.3 HWP products produced from domestic harvest
s: Equation 12.3 estimates the portion of HWP production made from domestically harvested wood using wood-flow ratios that include imports and exports of roundwood, chips and residues.

n: Equation 12.4 HWP from domestic harvest in domestic SWDS
s: Equation 12.4 approximates the domestic-harvest share of HWP carbon change in domestic SWDS by scaling Variable 1B with the non-imported share of wood material.

n: Equation 12.5 carbon release to the atmosphere from HWP variables
s: Equation 12.5 gives annual carbon release from HWP using the five HWP variables for domestic consumption and domestic harvest cases.

loc.section: METHOD D – COMBINE METHODS A, B AND C

n: Equation 12.6 for pre-1961 production, import and export variables
s: Equation 12.6 estimates production, imports or exports variables in Table 12.5 for years before 1961, but its formula is not included in the supplied units.

n: HWP Tier 1 backward extension of production, imports and exports before 1961
s: Estimates annual production, imports or exports of a solidwood or paper product for years before 1961 by exponential extrapolation from the 1961 value using a regional rate of change U.

n: Optional correction for CH4 double counting in landfill
s: Carbon released as methane from landfilled HWP can be subtracted from estimated carbon release to correct potential double counting.

loc.section: 1 All CO_2 released from HWP is included in the AFOLU Sector;

s: The Production Approach HWP contribution is computed from stock changes of domestically harvested HWP pools, or equivalently from harvest and domestically sourced HWP carbon release.
Under these guidelines the Simple Decay Approach HWP contribution is reported as −44/12 × (H − ↑C_HWP_DH), while a proposed alternative is still only a proposal.
Expresses annual AFOLU CO2 emissions as negative 44/12 times the summed annual carbon stock changes in AFOLU without HWP and in HWP pools.
Computes the HWP contribution to AFOLU net CO2 emissions from changes in carbon stocks of HWP in use and in SWDS, or equivalently from harvest, transfers and carbon release.
Tier 1 estimates the five HWP variables from FAO default activity data using first-order decay, with products-in-use inflows tracked from 1900 onward.

s: Variable 1B is estimated directly by the Waste Sector Tier 1 methods and spreadsheets, assuming HWP carbon equals garden, wood and paper waste categories.
