loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.45

n: Land converted to settlements annual biomass carbon change worksheet (3B5b)
s: The worksheet computes annual change in biomass carbon for land converted to settlements from area, pre-conversion biomass, carbon fraction, annual growth and annual biomass carbon loss.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.40

n: Land converted to settlements dead organic matter change worksheet (3B5b)
s: The worksheet computes annual change in dead wood and litter carbon from conversion area and the difference between new and old land-use carbon stocks divided by the transition period.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.41

n: Land converted to settlements mineral soil carbon change worksheet (3B5b)
s: The worksheet records mineral soil carbon change for land converted to settlements using reference carbon stocks, stock change factors and a default 20-year time period.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.42

s: Liming CO2-C emissions equal limestone mass times limestone emission factor plus dolomite mass times dolomite emission factor.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.54

n: Peatland N2O emissions from peat extraction worksheet (3B4bi)
s: The worksheet computes direct N2O emissions from peatlands managed for peat extraction as area times emission factor times the 44/28 conversion and a 10^-6 unit factor.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.37

n: Settlements remaining settlements organic soil carbon loss worksheet (3B5a)
s: The worksheet computes annual carbon loss from cultivated organic soils as land area times an emission factor for climate type.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.39

s: Urea fertilization CO2-C emissions equal annual urea amount times the urea emission factor.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.55

s: Annual carbon stock change for the entire AFOLU sector is the sum of changes across all land-use categories.

n: Animal manure N applied to soils (Equation 11.4)
s: Computes animal manure N applied to soils as managed manure N available net of fractions used for feed, fuel and construction.
Annual average population is computed from the number of animals produced annually and the days alive, divided by 365.
Annual decrease in biomass carbon in land remaining in the same category is the sum of wood removal, fuelwood and disturbance losses.

n: Annual carbon release from HWP stocks (Equation 12.5)
s: Annual carbon release is computed separately for wood stocks in the reporting country and for wood harvested domestically, using HWP flow and stock-change variables.

n: Annual change in HWP carbon in domestic SWDS from domestic harvest (Equation 12.4)
s: The domestic-harvest share of the annual change in HWP carbon in domestic SWDS is the total domestic change scaled by one minus the ratio of produced to total wood material.

n: Annual CO2 emissions from urea application (Equation 11.13)
s: Annual carbon emission from urea application equals the annual urea amount times an emission factor.

n: Annual N excretion from default N excretion rate (Equation 10.30)
s: Computes annual N excretion per animal from a default daily N excretion rate scaled by typical animal mass and 365 days.

n: Annual N excretion from N intake and retention (Equation 10.31, Tier 2)
s: Computes annual N excretion as N intake multiplied by one minus the fraction of intake retained by the animal.

n: Average annual biomass growth (Tier 1 and Tiers 2–3)
s: Mean annual biomass growth G_TOTAL is taken directly from dry-matter increment data at Tier 1, or from net annual increment times BCEF_I times (1+R) at Tiers 2 and 3.

n: BCEF_S from BEF_S and wood density
s: When BCEF_S is unavailable, it may be computed as BEF_S times basic wood density D.

n: Biomass carbon gain from mean annual biomass growth (Equation 2.9)
s: Annual increase in biomass carbon from growth equals area times mean annual biomass growth times carbon fraction, summed over ecological zones and climate domains.

n: Biomass carbon stock change by stock difference (Equation 2.8)
s: Annual change in biomass carbon for land remaining in the same category is the difference in total biomass carbon between t_1 and t_2 divided by elapsed time.

n: Biomass carbon total from volume, expansion and carbon fraction (Equation 2.8 total carbon term)
s: Total biomass carbon for a land sub-category is the sum over strata of area times merchantable growing stock volume times BCEF_S times (1+R) times carbon fraction.
Annual change in biomass carbon in land remaining in a land-use category equals biomass growth gain minus biomass loss over the total area.

n: Biomass change on converted land (Equation 2.15, Tier 2)
s: Annual change in biomass carbon on converted land equals growth plus initial conversion change minus losses.
Annual biomass carbon loss due to disturbances equals disturbed area times average above-ground biomass times (1+R) times carbon fraction times fraction of biomass lost.
Annual carbon loss from fuelwood equals whole-tree fuelwood volume times BCEF_R times (1+R) plus tree-part fuelwood volume times basic wood density, times carbon fraction.
Annual carbon loss from wood removals equals roundwood removal volume times BCEF_R times (1+R) times carbon fraction.
Computes daily N retained by cattle from milk protein N and weight-gain N, where weight-gain N uses net energy for growth and fixed NRC constants.
Annual change in carbon stocks in dead organic matter equals the sum of dead wood and litter changes.

n: Direct N2O emissions from managed soils, Tier 1 (Equation 11.1)
s: Sums direct N2O-N from N inputs, organic soils and pasture urine and dung deposition.

n: Direct N2O emissions from managed soils, Tier 2 (Equation 11.2)
s: Sums direct N2O-N from condition-specific N inputs, crop residues, soil mineralisation, organic soils and pasture deposition.

n: direct N2O emissions from manure management (Equation 10.25)
s: Direct N2O from manure is the sum over systems of N excretion times manure fraction times EF3, converted from N2O-N by 44/28.

n: Dry-weight correction of reported crop yields (Equation 11.7)
s: Converts harvested fresh yield to dry matter yield by multiplying by the dry matter fraction.
Enteric CH4 emission factor per head is derived from gross energy intake and methane conversion factor using 55.65 MJ/kg CH4.
Enteric CH4 emissions for a livestock category are the emission factor times head count, scaled to Gg.

n: Equation 2.18 gain-loss method for dead wood or litter carbon change
s: Annual change in dead wood/litter carbon equals managed area times the difference between DOM inputs and outputs times carbon fraction.

n: Equation 2.20 annual carbon in biomass transferred to dead organic matter
s: Total carbon transferred from biomass to dead organic matter is the sum of mortality, slash and disturbance-left-to-decay components.

n: Equation 2.21 annual biomass carbon loss due to mortality
s: Mortality carbon loss equals the sum over land of area times above-ground biomass growth times carbon fraction times mortality rate.

n: Equation 2.22 annual carbon transfer to slash
s: Carbon transferred to slash from harvest is computed from harvest volume, biomass conversion factor, root-shoot ratio, wood density, and carbon fraction.

n: Equation 2.27 greenhouse gas emissions from fire
s: Fire emissions equal burnt area times fuel mass times combustion factor times emission factor times 10^-3.

n: Equation 5.2 adjusted daily emission factor for rice
s: Adjusted daily CH4 emission factor is the baseline factor multiplied by water regime, pre-season, organic amendment and soil/cultivar scaling factors.
Wetland CO2 emissions are the sum of peatland and flooded land emissions.

n: Equation 7.7 direct N2O emissions from peatlands during peat extraction
s: Direct N2O from peat extraction equals drained nutrient-rich peat area times N2O-N emission factor times 44/28 times 10^-6.

n: Extrapolation of pre-1961 production, imports or exports (Equation 12.6)
s: Production, import or export values for years before 1961 are estimated by exponential extrapolation from the 1961 value using a regional rate of change.

n: Gain-loss method for annual carbon stock change (Equation 2.4)
s: Annual carbon stock change in a pool equals annual carbon gain minus annual carbon loss.

n: HWP inflow from production, imports and exports (Equation 12.2)
s: Carbon in annual domestic consumption of HWP equals production plus semi-finished imports minus semi-finished exports.

n: HWP pool carbon stock change by first-order decay (Equation 12.1)
s: The annual carbon stock change of the HWP pool is computed year by year from the stock at the beginning of each year, with the stock starting at zero in 1900.
Carbon in annual production of HWP from domestically harvested wood is production scaled by the ratio of net roundwood, chip and residue flows.

n: Imported wood material composition for HWP SWDS split (Equation 12.4 denominator)
s: Imported wood material is the sum of selected roundwood, chip, residue, sawnwood, panel, paper and pulp import flows.

n: Indirect N2O emissions due to leaching and runoff from manure management (Equation 10.29)
s: Computes indirect N2O from leached and runoff manure N as N_leaching-MMS multiplied by EF5 and scaled by 44/28.

n: Indirect N2O emissions from volatilisation of N from manure management (Equation 10.27)
s: Computes indirect N2O emissions from volatilised manure nitrogen in manure management systems as the volatilised N multiplied by EF4 and scaled by 44/28.

n: Indirect N2O from atmospheric deposition of volatilised N, Tier 1 (Equation 11.9)
s: Computes indirect N2O-N from NH3 and NOx volatilised from synthetic fertiliser, organic N and urine/dung N, multiplied by EF4.

n: Indirect N2O from leaching and runoff in regions where it occurs, Tier 1 (Equation 11.10)
s: Computes indirect N2O-N from leached and runoff N additions in regions where leaching or runoff occurs, multiplied by EF5.

n: Initial biomass carbon change on converted land (Equation 2.16)
s: Initial biomass carbon change on land converted to another category is the sum over land types of biomass change at conversion times area converted, times carbon fraction.

n: Land-use category carbon stock change as sum of strata (Equation 2.2)
s: Annual carbon stock change for a land-use category is the sum of changes over its strata i = 1 to n.

n: Limestone and dolomite CO2-C emission from lime application
s: Annual carbon emission from lime application is the sum of limestone and dolomite amounts times their emission factors.

n: Managed manure N available for application, feed, fuel or construction (Equation 10.34)
s: Computes managed manure N available for soils, feed, fuel or construction from livestock N excretion net of manure N losses, plus bedding N, summed over categories and systems.
Annual CH4 emission factor for manure is computed from volatile solids, maximum methane capacity and weighted methane conversion factors.
Manure nitrogen lost to NH3 and NOx volatilisation is computed per management system from N excretion, system fraction and a gas loss fraction.

n: Mineralised N in mineral soils from soil carbon loss (Equation 11.8)
s: Converts average annual soil carbon loss to net mineralised N using the soil organic matter C:N ratio.

n: N from crop residues and forage/pasture renewal (Equation 11.6)
s: Sums above-ground and below-ground crop residue N returned to soils, with above-ground residue reduced by the removed fraction.

n: N in urine and dung deposited by grazing animals (Equation 11.5)
s: Sums livestock N excretion deposited on pasture, range and paddock across categories.

n: N losses due to leaching from manure management systems (Equation 10.28)
s: Sums managed manure N multiplied by Frac_leachMS over livestock categories and manure management systems to give N leached from manure management systems.

n: N volatilisation from manure management systems (Equation 10.26)
s: Sums, over livestock categories and manure management systems, managed manure N multiplied by Frac_GasMS to give N volatilised as NH3 and NOx.
Non-CO2 emissions equal activity data multiplied by an emission factor.

n: Permanently flooded land biomass carbon change method
s: Annual biomass carbon change on land converted to flooded land is the area-weighted sum of biomass change multiplied by carbon fraction.

n: Settlements biomass increment by crown cover area (Equation 8.2)
s: Annual carbon accumulation from biomass increment in Settlements is the sum over crown cover classes and woody perennial types of total crown cover area times crown-cover-based growth rate.

n: Settlements biomass increment by number of individual woody plants (Equation 8.3)
s: Annual carbon accumulation from live biomass increment in Settlements is the sum over classes of number of individuals times annual average carbon accumulation per individual.
Annual carbon accumulation in live biomass in Settlements Remaining Settlements is the sum of tree, shrub and herbaceous biomass increments.

n: Stock-difference method for annual carbon stock change (Equation 2.5)
s: Annual carbon stock change in a pool is the difference between carbon stock estimates at two times divided by the elapsed time.

n: Stratum carbon stock change as sum of pool changes (Equation 2.3)
s: Annual carbon stock change for a stratum is the sum of changes in above-ground biomass, below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter, soils and harvested wood products.
Total enteric fermentation CH4 is the sum of emissions across livestock categories and subcategories.

n: Total organic N applied to soils (Equation 11.3)
s: Sums animal manure, sewage, compost and other organic amendment N applied to soils.
Daily volatile solid excretion is computed from gross energy, digestibility, urinary energy and ash content.

n: Level 1 CO2 diffusive emission equation for land converted to flooded land (Equation 2a.1)
s: Level 1 estimates annual CO2 emissions from land converted to flooded land as the product of ice-free days, averaged daily diffusive emission factor, total reservoir surface area, fraction flooded within the last 10 years, and a 10^-6 unit conversion.

loc.section: CO_2 Emissions_LWflood = P • E (CO_2 )_diff • A_flood_,_total __ _surface • f _A • 10^−^6

n: Level 2 CO2 diffusive emission equation with ice-free and ice-covered periods (Equation 2a.2)
s: Level 2 estimates annual CO2 diffusive emissions from land converted to flooded land by summing ice-free and ice-covered period diffusive emissions weighted by their day counts, multiplied by surface area fraction flooded in the last 10 years and a 10^-6 conversion factor.
Tier 1 estimates total CH4 emissions from flooded land by multiplying the ice-free period, averaged daily diffusive emission factor and total flooded surface area, with a 10^-6 unit conversion.
Tier 2 sums diffusive and bubble emissions over ice-free and ice-covered periods using country-specific factors and flooded surface area.

n: Chapter 2 data collection guidance for solid waste management
s: Chapter 2 gives general guidance on data collection for solid waste management; it is referenced here but its content is not in this batch.

n: MSW generation and management default data (regional defaults, Table 2.1)
s: Regional default per-capita MSW generation rates and management fractions for the year 2000 are tabulated in Table 2.1 and are intended as Tier 1 inputs.

n: Waste stream analysis for DOCm disposed at SWDS
s: Waste stream analysis tracks mass, moisture and DOCm of each waste type through treatment steps to estimate DOCm disposed at SWDS, with reduction rates applied at each process.
The 1996 Guidelines compute yearly decomposition as the rate-of-reaction value at year end, which approximates the integral by rectangles and neglects the triangles above the columns.

n: 3 个月延迟的年份分解 (3A1.8，处置年)
s: With a 3-month delay the DDOCm decomposed in the disposal year equals DDOCm times one minus e^(-0.25k).
CH4 emitted in year T equals the sum of CH4 generated minus CH4 recovered, multiplied by (1 minus oxidation factor).
Annual CH4 emissions from solid waste disposal are computed as the sum of CH4 generated minus recovered CH4, multiplied by (1 minus oxidation factor).

n: DDOCm accumulated at end of year T (Equation 3.4)
s: DDOCm accumulated at year end equals DDOCm deposited in year T plus the previous year's accumulated DDOCm multiplied by e^-k.

n: DDOCm 分解与 CH4 生成换算 (3A1.16–3A1.17)
s: Decomposable DOCm entering the SWDS is waste mass times DOC, DOC_f and MCF, and CH4 generated equals decomposed DDOCm times F times 16/12.

n: DDOCm decomposed at end of year T (Equation 3.5)
s: DDOCm decomposed in year T equals accumulated DDOCm at end of year T−1 times (1 minus e^-k).

n: Decomposable DOC from waste disposal data (Equation 3.2)
s: Mass of decomposable DOC deposited equals waste mass times degradable organic carbon fraction, times decomposable fraction, times MCF.

n: Direct measurement from gas collection systems to estimate FOD parameters
s: Estimates FOD model parameters (such as decay rate and CH4 generation potential) from statistical fitting of gas collection system measurements over a representative landfill database.

loc.section: 3.3 USE OF MEASUREMENT IN THE ESTIMATION OF CH_4 EMISSIONS FROM SWDS

n: Direct measurement of CH4 emissions from SWDS surface
s: Surface CH4 emission measurement methods (flux chamber, mass balance, micrometeorological, plume) with stated strengths, limitations and no agreed preferred method as of 2006.
DOC of bulk waste is a weighted average of degradable carbon fractions of waste types, weighted by their waste-category fractions.

n: 长期储存 DOCm 计算 (3A1.19)
s: Long-term stored DOCm equals waste disposed times DOC times one minus DOC_f times MCF.

n: First order decay (FOD) model basic equation
s: The FOD model gives remaining degradable organic carbon mass as an exponential decay of its initial value over time.

n: 精确日级 FOD 与递推 (3A1.23–3A1.25)
s: The exact FOD model is shown equivalent to a disposal at a single point in each year, with a recursive formulation for stock and CH4 generation given a delay Δ between 0 and 1 year.

n: FOD 年度分解 (3A1.9，年内延迟 3 个月)
s: Under a 3-month delay the decomposed DDOCm in year T is computed from the difference of two exponentials, where T is years after disposal.

n: FOD 年度分解 DDOCm 方程 (3A1.10–3A1.11, 产生始于次年1月1日)
s: The spreadsheet FOD recursion computes DDOCm accumulated and decomposed each year, assuming decay starts on 1 January of the year after disposal.

n: FOD decomposed DDOCm after one year
s: The amount of DDOCm decomposed by the end of year 1 equals the initial DDOCm_0 times one minus e^-k.
The GPG2000 equation integrates the decay curve but starts year 1 from point 1 to point 2, so first-year CH4 is not counted and results are about 7 percent low at a 10-year half-life.

n: Half-life selection approaches for FOD model
s: Two alternative approaches select half-life: a weighted average for mixed MSW (bulk waste option) or per-category half-lives assumed independent (waste composition option).

n: Half-life to decay rate constant relation
s: The decay rate constant k equals ln(2) divided by the half-life.

n: 延迟 M 个月的 DDOCm 分解 (3A1.12–3A1.15)
s: For a reaction start with delay M months, DDOCm remaining and decomposed in the disposal year are computed using exponents involving (13−M)/12.

n: Methane recovery efficiency estimation from number of SWDS or capacity
s: Indirect CH4 recovery estimates based on number of SWDS with gas recovery or on utilisation/flare capacity, with stated default assumptions and cautions.
CH4 generation potential L_o equals DDOCm times CH4 volume fraction F times the 16/12 CH4/C molecular weight ratio.
Waste generation is the product of per capita generation rate and population, and activity data also include the fraction of waste disposed to SWDS.

n: Equation 4.1 CH4 emissions from biological treatment
s: Estimates annual CH4 emissions from biological treatment as the sum over treatment types of mass times emission factor, times 10^-3, minus recovered CH4.

n: Equation 4.2 N2O emissions from biological treatment
s: Estimates annual N2O emissions from biological treatment as the sum over treatment types of mass times emission factor, times 10^-3.

n: Equation 5.1 CO2 emission estimate based on total amount of waste combusted
s: Estimates fossil CO2 emissions from incineration or open burning by multiplying each waste type's wet-weight amount by dry matter, carbon content, fossil carbon fraction and oxidation factor, then converting C to CO2 with 44/12.

n: Equation 5.2 CO2 emission estimate based on MSW composition
s: Estimates fossil CO2 emissions from MSW incineration or open burning by summing material-specific fractions of MSW multiplied by dry matter, carbon, fossil carbon fraction and oxidation factor, then converting to CO2 with 44/12.

n: Equation 5.3 CO2 emission from incineration of fossil liquid waste
s: CO2 emissions from incineration of fossil liquid waste are estimated as the sum over waste types of amount times carbon content times oxidation factor, multiplied by 44/12.

n: Equation 5.4 CH4 emission estimate based on total amount of waste combusted
s: CH4 emissions from incineration or open burning are estimated as the sum over waste types of amount times aggregate CH4 emission factor, multiplied by 10^-6.

n: Equation 5.5 N2O emission estimate based on waste input to incinerators
s: N2O emissions are estimated as the sum over waste types of waste input times a default N2O emission factor, multiplied by 10^-6.

n: Equation 5.6 N2O emission estimate based on flue gas measurements
s: Tier 3 N2O emissions are estimated from waste amount, flue gas N2O concentration and flue gas volume per unit waste, multiplied by 10^-9.

n: Equation 5.7 total municipal solid waste open-burned
s: The total amount of municipal solid waste open-burned is population times fraction burning times per capita waste generation times fraction burned times 365 days, converted to Gg.

n: MSW化石碳比例加权计算式 (Equation 5.10)
s: Total fossil carbon fraction in MSW is the weighted sum of waste type fractions times their fossil carbon fractions.

n: MSW干物质含量加权计算式 (Equation 5.8)
s: Total dry matter content in MSW is computed as the weighted sum of component fractions times their dry matter contents.
Total carbon content in MSW is the weighted sum of component fractions times their carbon contents.

n: CH4 emission factor for industrial wastewater (Equation 6.5)
s: Industrial wastewater CH4 emission factor is the product of maximum CH4 producing capacity B_o and the methane correction factor MCF_j for each treatment or discharge pathway.
Domestic wastewater CH4 emissions are computed as the sum over income groups and pathways of U_i × T_i,j × EF_j, multiplied by (TOW − S), minus recovered CH4 R.
The emission factor for each domestic wastewater treatment or discharge pathway equals the maximum CH4 producing capacity B_o multiplied by the methane correction factor MCF_j.
The chapter lists a three-step good-practice procedure for domestic wastewater CH4 that uses Equations 6.1 to 6.3.

n: N2O emissions from centralized wastewater treatment plants (Equation 6.9)
s: Plant N2O emissions equal population times degree of utilization of centralized plants times the industrial-commercial co-discharge factor times the per-person plant emission factor.
Annual N2O emissions from effluent equal effluent nitrogen times the emission factor times 44/28.

n: Organically degradable material in industrial wastewater (Equation 6.6)
s: Total organically degradable material in industrial wastewater for sector i is the product of total industrial product P_i, wastewater generation W_i and COD_i.

n: Total CH4 emissions from industrial wastewater (Equation 6.4)
s: Industrial wastewater CH4 emissions are summed over industrial sectors i as (TOW_i − S_i) × EF_i minus recovered R_i, using COD units.
Effluent nitrogen is population times protein consumption times nitrogen fraction times non-consumed and industrial co-discharge factors, minus nitrogen removed with sludge.

n: Total organically degradable material in domestic wastewater (Equation 6.3)
s: TOW is calculated from population, country-specific per capita BOD, a g-to-kg conversion, an industrial correction factor I and 365 days.

n: Worksheet 4B CH4 emissions from Biological Treatment of Solid Waste
s: The worksheet computes net annual CH4 emissions from biological treatment as gross generation (A x B x 10^-3) minus recovered/flared methane.

n: Worksheet 4B N2O emissions from Biological Treatment of Solid Waste
s: The worksheet computes net annual N2O emissions from biological treatment as amount treated times emission factor, scaled by 10^-3.

n: Worksheet 4C1 CH4 emissions from Incineration of Waste
s: The worksheet computes CH4 from incineration as incinerated wet-weight amount times a methane emission factor, scaled by 10^-6 to Gg.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.8

n: Worksheet 4C1 CO2 emissions from incineration of fossil liquid waste
s: The worksheet computes fossil CO2 from incinerated fossil liquid waste as weight times fossil carbon content, oxidation factor and 44/12.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.6

n: Worksheet 4C1 CO2 emissions from Incineration of Waste (fossil CO2)
s: The worksheet computes fossil CO2 from incinerated waste as the product of wet-weight amount, dry matter fraction, carbon fraction, fossil carbon fraction, oxidation factor and the 44/12 conversion.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.4

n: Worksheet 4C1 N2O emissions from Incineration of Waste
s: The worksheet computes N2O from incineration as wet-weight amount times a nitrous oxide emission factor, scaled by 10^-6 to Gg.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.10

n: Worksheet 4C2 CH4 emissions from Open Burning of Waste
s: The worksheet computes CH4 from open burning as open-burned wet-weight amount times a methane emission factor, scaled by 10^-6 to Gg.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.8

n: Worksheet 4C2 CO2 emissions from Open Burning of Waste (fossil CO2)
s: The worksheet computes fossil CO2 from open-burned waste as open-burned amount times dry matter, carbon, fossil carbon, oxidation factor and 44/12 conversion.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.6

n: Worksheet 4C2 N2O emissions from Open Burning of Waste
s: The worksheet computes N2O from open burning as dry-weight amount times a nitrous oxide emission factor, scaled by 10^-6 to Gg.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.10

n: Worksheet 4C2 total amount of waste open-burned
s: The worksheet estimates total MSW open-burned as population times burning fraction times per-capita waste generation times burned fraction times days per year, scaled by 10^-6.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.4

n: Worksheet 4D1 CH4 emission factor for domestic wastewater
s: The worksheet computes the CH4 emission factor for each domestic treatment system as maximum methane producing capacity times the methane correction factor.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.12

n: Worksheet 4D1 CH4 emissions from domestic wastewater
s: The worksheet computes net CH4 emissions per income group and pathway as emission factor times TOW minus sludge removed, minus recovered methane.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.14

n: Worksheet 4D1 indirect N2O emissions from wastewater
s: The worksheet computes indirect N2O emissions from wastewater as effluent nitrogen times emission factor times 44/28, minus emissions from wastewater plants.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.18

s: The worksheet computes total nitrogen in domestic effluent as population times protein consumption times nitrogen fraction times non-consumption fraction times industrial co-discharge fraction, minus sludge nitrogen.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.18

n: Worksheet 4D1 organically degradable material in domestic wastewater
s: The worksheet computes organically degradable material in domestic wastewater as population times BOD per capita times an industrial correction factor.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.12

n: Worksheet 4D2 CH4 emissions from industrial wastewater
s: The worksheet computes net CH4 emissions for each industrial sector as (TOW minus sludge removed) times emission factor, minus recovered methane.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.16

n: Worksheet 4D2 total organic degradable material in industrial wastewater
s: The worksheet computes total organic degradable material in wastewater for each industry sector as product output times wastewater generated times COD concentration.

loc.section: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories A1.14

s: CO2-equivalent emission is most typically obtained by multiplying a GHG emission by its 100-year global warming potential.
The coefficient of variation is the ratio of population standard deviation to population mean.
The correlation coefficient is a number between -1 and +1 measuring the mutual relationship of two observed variables.
The Monte Carlo method analyses inventory uncertainty by repeatedly computing the inventory with randomly sampled uncertain inputs.
Quality Assurance is a planned review system conducted by personnel not directly involved in inventory compilation to verify data quality objectives.
Quality Control is a routine technical system to measure and control inventory quality during development.
Reporting is the process of providing inventory results as described in Volume 1 Chapter 8.
An uncertainty analysis quantifies output uncertainty caused by model uncertainty and input uncertainty and examines the relative importance of these factors.
In emission inventories, validation checks that the inventory was compiled correctly per reporting instructions and its internal consistency.

n: Facility data integration equations (2019 Refinement Chapter 2)
s: The annex lists four new facility-data equations in Chapter 2 but the equation formulas are not reproduced in this mapping table.

n: Key category Level and Trend Assessment (Approach 1)
s: Chapter 4 retains Approach 1 level and trend assessment equations for identifying key categories, with the trend equation simplified in the 2019 Refinement.

n: Aggregation of confidential data by category
s: Confidential facility-level emissions may be aggregated into sector or category totals, with categories chosen to suit national circumstances, so the data stay confidential.
Available facility data should be assessed on transparency, IPCC method consistency, QA/QC and uncertainty, and representativeness and consistency with national data.

loc.section: 2.3.4 Uses of facility data not originally designed for inventory application

n: E_IC total facility emissions by industrial classification (Equation 2.4)
s: Total emissions for an industry classification are the sum over IPCC source categories s of the emissions for that classification and source.

n: Emissions calculated by facility-specific emission factors (Equation 2.2)
s: Emissions for an industrial classification are calculated by multiplying national activity data for each source by a facility-based emission factor developed from FRD.
When no data exist, experts estimate missing data using inputs such as similar-country reports, regional information, correlated variables, source existence checks, and order-of-magnitude estimates.

n: Facility data integration by emission source (Equation 2.3)
s: Total emissions for an industrial classification combine residual national activity data multiplied by a facility-based emission factor with directly reported facility emissions.
A decision tree assesses FRD quality, completeness and national consistency before selecting an integration approach using Equations 2.1, 2.2 or 2.3.

loc.section: Figure 2.3 (New) Sample decision tree for integration of FRD

s: Facility data not designed for inventories should be assessed for methodology, quality and documentation, and facility-specific methods not meeting recognised standards should be used only if assured to be equivalent or better.
A reliable measurement programme requires a stated objective, methodology protocol, measurement plan with instructions, and data processing and reporting documentation.

n: Grand total emissions by industry classification (Equation 2.4)
s: The grand total for an industry classification is obtained by summing Equation 2.3 results over all sources and activities.
Panels of constant small household samples can monitor municipal waste generation and composition over time, but require paid participation, which limits use.

n: Landfill and incinerator waste generation per inhabitant estimate
s: Waste generated per inhabitant can be approximately derived from controlled landfill disposal or incinerator capacity together with served population or area.

n: Municipal waste collection vehicle weighing sampling
s: The most common municipal waste estimation method weighs a representative sample of collection vehicles before and after collection and grosses up to the whole population.
Even with partial coverage, facility data may derive country-specific emission factors, check inventory estimates, derive proxies, or fill gaps under stated conditions.

s: The residual national activity data not covered by facility reporting is obtained by subtracting the facility-reported activity data from the national activity dataset.
Surrogate data correlated with missing activity data may be used via a country-specific regression factor, after documenting physical relationship and statistical correlation.

n: Total facility emissions from all sources (Equation 2.1)
s: Total reported facility emissions equal the sum of energy, fugitive, process and other source emissions, excluding de minimis where applicable.

n: 95 percent confidence interval uncertainty from sigma
s: The source gives a formula for the 95 percent uncertainty of a parameter using the standard deviation σ and mean µ.
The chapter presents two approaches for combining category uncertainties into uncertainty estimates for total national net emissions and trends, with Approach 1 being simpler.

n: Approach 1 误差传播：乘积不确定度（Equation 3.1）
s: Approach 1 gives the percentage uncertainty of a product of uncorrelated quantities by combining their percentage uncertainties in a root-sum-of-squares form, which is approximate and reasonable when percentage uncertainties are below about 30%.

n: Approach 1 误差传播：加减法不确定度（Equation 3.2）
s: Approach 1 gives the percentage uncertainty of a sum or difference of uncorrelated quantities, which is exact for uncorrelated variables.

n: Approach 1 排放量不确定度：活动数据×排放因子（Equation 3.2a）
s: For a simple category emission estimated as activity data times emission factor with uncorrelated inputs, the percentage uncertainty of emissions is the root sum of squares of the activity data and emission factor uncertainties.

n: Approach 1 排放因子不确定度：多参数乘积（Equation 3.2b）
s: When an emission factor is the product of several uncorrelated parameters a, b and c, its percentage uncertainty is the root sum of squares of the individual parameter uncertainties.

n: Approach 1 趋势不确定度分项（Equations 3.2f 与 3.2g）
s: Approach 1 propagates emission factor uncertainty to the trend through a Type A sensitivity, assuming fully correlated emission factors across years, and activity data uncertainty through a Type B sensitivity with a factor of √2, assuming independent activity data across years.
Worked example in which category-level uncertainties (AD, EF/parameter, combined, variance contribution, sensitivities) are tabulated for Finland's inventory to illustrate Approach 1.
Approach 1 worksheet combines activity data and emission factor uncertainties by category via error propagation and computes trend uncertainty from sensitivities.
Approach 2 of the 2006 Guidelines combines uncertainties by Monte Carlo simulation; this batch shows only its section heading with no refinement text.

n: Approach 2 Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis for CH4 enteric fermentation (Italian example)
s: Step-by-step Monte Carlo example, based on the Italian inventory, that selects parameters, assigns distributions, runs 5,000 trials and ranks parameter sensitivity for CH4 from enteric fermentation.

n: Conversion of EF range to percentage uncertainty
s: The source gives formulas to convert a minimum and maximum emission factor range, assumed to contain 95 percent of values, into lower and upper percentage uncertainty.

The generic uncertainty assessment process has four parts: investigating causes of uncertainty, quantifying uncertainty and correlations, mathematically combining estimates, and selecting improvement actions.

s: The source gives the standard deviation formula using n in the denominator as an approximation for large samples.
The source gives the standard error formula for the uncertainty of a sample mean, used when the mean estimates the whole population.

n: Trend uncertainty propagation in Approach 1 (Columns M to Q)
s: Approach 1 computes Type A and Type B sensitivities and propagates emission factor and activity data uncertainties into the trend, with the sqrt(2) factor applied when uncertainties are uncorrelated across years.

n: Type A and Type B sensitivity (Table 3.2 Notes)
s: Type A sensitivity captures systematic error correlated across years and Type B sensitivity captures random error affecting only the current year.
Level assessment computes each category's share of the total sum of absolute emission and removal estimates in the latest inventory year.
Approach 1 level assessment ranks categories by their absolute emissions share of the total inventory to identify key categories, as illustrated for Finland 2016.
Trend assessment measures the change in each category's estimate between the base year and the latest year, relative to the total inventory change.
Approach 1 trend assessment measures each category's contribution to the change in total inventory emissions between a base year and the current year, as illustrated for Finland 1990 to 2016.

n: Approach 2 level assessment (key category analysis, uncertainty-weighted)
s: Approach 2 level assessment weights each category's absolute emissions by its uncertainty in emissions to rank key categories, as illustrated for Finland 2016.

n: Approach 2 trend assessment (key category analysis, uncertainty-weighted)
s: Approach 2 trend assessment incorporates category uncertainty into the trend contribution to rank key categories by trend, as illustrated for Finland 1990 to 2016.
For a gap, the average annual change between the last year before and first year after the gap is added cumulatively to fill each gap year.

n: Linear interpolation for time series gaps
s: Intermediate years are estimated by interpolating between detailed estimates, assuming constant annual growth, appropriate only for stable trends.
For multiplicative trends, a least-squares polynomial fitted to known data points is used to impute missing years, with the order chosen as the lowest adequate fit.

The overlap technique builds a time series for years when a new method cannot be used by proportionally adjusting previously developed estimates using the relationship observed during the overlap period, with the estimate given by Equation 5.1.
Recalculated estimate is obtained by multiplying the previously used method estimate by the ratio of summed new-method to summed old-method estimates over the overlap years m to n.

n: Ratio-based correction factor for overlap case study (Box 5.1b, methane from charcoal production)
s: Tier 2 to Tier 1 ratios over 2004-2010 are averaged (0.93) and used to correct Tier 1 estimates for missing years 2001-2003.
Missing time-series values are estimated from correlated indicative data such as GDP or population when emission parameters correlate strongly with those data.

s: Australia's annual SF6 loss rate from electricity supply and distribution is calibrated to changes in atmospheric SF6 concentrations measured at Cape Grim using interspecies correlation and inverse modelling.

s: Greenhouse gas emissions from underground coal mines equal raw coal production times an emission factor times a units conversion factor, before adjustment for methane utilisation or flaring.

s: Fugitive emissions from oil product distribution are the sum of gasoline and other product consumption volumes times their emission factors.

n: Tier 1 fugitive GHG emission from coke production (Equation 4.3.2)

n: Tier 1 post-mining methane emissions, surface mines (Equation 4.1.8)

n: Tier 1 surface mine CH4 and CO2 emissions (Equations 4.1.7 and 4.1.7 A)

n: Tier 1 underground mining CO2 emissions (Equation 4.1.3 A)
s: Tier 1 estimates underground coal mine CO2 emissions as CO2 emission factor times underground coal production times conversion factor.

n: Tier 1 underground mining methane emission factor
s: The Tier 1 low-case emission factor for underground coal mining methane is 10 m3 per tonne of coal, the same values used in the Revised 1996 IPCC Guidelines.

n: Tier 2 abandoned mine emission factor decline curve (Equation 4.1.12)
s: The Tier 2 dimensionless emission factor follows (1 + aT) raised to b, where a and b are decline curve constants and T is years since abandonment.

n: Tier 2 abandoned underground mine emissions without recovery (Equation 4.1.11)
s: Tier 2 methane emissions equal unflooded abandoned mine count times gassy fraction times average emission rate times emission factor times conversion factor, excluding recovery and utilization.

n: Tier 2 basin-specific method for coal exploration boreholes (Equation 4Ap.1.2)
s: Tier 2 sums basin-level emissions, each being a basin emission factor times the number of exploration boreholes drilled in that basin times a conversion factor.

n: Tier 2 post-mining emission factor from in situ gas content
s: Tier 2 post-mining emission factor is 30 percent of in situ gas content without pre-drainage and 10 percent with pre-drainage.

n: Equation 2.1 AFOLU annual carbon stock change
s: Annual carbon stock change for the AFOLU sector is the sum of changes across all land-use categories.

n: Equation 2.18 Annual change in carbon stocks in dead wood or litter (gain-loss method)
s: Annual change in dead wood or litter carbon is computed from DOM inputs and outputs, area and carbon fraction, per the gain-loss method.

n: Equation 2.19 Annual change in carbon stocks in dead wood or litter (stock-difference method)
s: Annual change in dead wood or litter carbon equals the difference between two stock estimates divided by the interval, times area and carbon fraction.

n: Equation 2.2 land-use category carbon stock change as sum over strata
s: Annual carbon stock change for a land-use category is the sum of changes in each stratum within the category.

n: Equation 2.20 Annual carbon in biomass transferred to dead organic matter
s: Carbon transferred to dead organic matter is the sum of mortality and slash transfers plus the fraction of disturbance losses left to decay on the ground.

n: Equation 2.21 Annual biomass carbon loss due to mortality
s: Mortality transfer to DOM is computed from area, above-ground biomass growth, carbon fraction and mortality rate.

loc.section: Transfers to dead organic matter from mortality, L_mortality

n: Equation 2.22 Annual carbon transfer to slash
s: Slash carbon transfer is derived from harvest volume, wood density, expansion factors, root-to-shoot ratio and carbon fraction.

n: Equation 2.23 Annual change in carbon stocks in dead wood and litter due to land conversion
s: Land-conversion DOM change is the difference between new and old land-use stocks times converted area divided by the transition period.

n: Equation 2.24 annual change in soil carbon stocks
s: Sums annual change in soil carbon stocks from mineral soils, organic soils and inorganic carbon.

n: Equation 2.25 annual change in organic carbon stocks in mineral soils (ΔC_Mineral)
s: Computes annual change in mineral soil organic carbon stock over an inventory period using stock change factors and reference stocks summed over climate zones, soil types and management systems.

n: Equation 2.27 Estimation of greenhouse gas emissions from fire
s: IPCC Equation 2.27 estimates greenhouse gas emissions from fire as the product of area burnt, fuel biomass consumption (MB), combustion factor (Cf) and emission factor (Gef), scaled by 10^-3.

n: Equation 2.3 stratum carbon stock change as sum over pools
s: Annual carbon stock change for a stratum is the sum of changes in all carbon pools including harvested wood products.

n: Equation 2.4 Gain-Loss Method for annual carbon stock change in a pool
s: Annual carbon stock change in a pool is estimated as annual gains minus annual losses, with gains positive and losses negative.

n: Remote sensing digital vs visual land classification
s: Land cover can be classified by visual or digital analysis, each with trade-offs in human inference, scalability and automation.

n: Standard deviation derivation for Table 4.11 MAI values
s: For Table 4.11, the standard deviation is estimated from the reported min and max MAI values.

n: Tier 1 forest soil carbon stock change (mineral soils)
s: Tier 1 assumes forest soil carbon stocks do not change with management, so stock change factors equal 1 and only reference stocks are needed.

n: Tier 1 mineral soil stock change calculation steps for Land Converted to Forest Land
s: Seven-step procedure for estimating initial and final soil organic carbon stocks and net mineral soil C stock change per hectare for Land Converted to Forest Land under Tier 1.

n: Tier 1 worked example: afforestation of cropland soil (100,000 ha)
s: Numerical example computing initial SOC, annual soil C change and total annual increase for 100,000 ha of cropland converted to forest.

n: Tier 2 forest soil organic carbon stock calculation
s: Tier 2 computes soil organic C stocks from reference soil C stocks and country-specific stock change factors for forest type, management and natural disturbance regime.
Active sub-pool SOC stock for year y is computed from previous-year stock, steady-state stock, and the active pool decay rate over one year.

n: Adjusted daily CH4 emission factor EFi
s: Adjusted daily CH4 emission factor for rice is the product of baseline EFc and the water-regime, pre-season and organic-amendment scaling factors.

n: Adjusted daily emission factor for rice (Tier 1, Equation 5.2)
s: Adjusted daily emission factor is the baseline continuously flooded emission factor multiplied by water-regime, pre-season water-regime and organic amendment scaling factors.

n: Average annual SOC change formula (Tier 1 step 8)
s: Average annual change in soil organic C equals final minus initial SOC stock divided by the time dependence of the stock change factors.

n: Bayesian parameterisation of Tier 2 steady-state method for mineral soils
s: Probability distributions of the most sensitive Tier 2 steady-state parameters are estimated by sampling-importance resampling with uniform priors.

n: C input to the active sub-pool (Equation 5.0g)
s: The C input to the active sub-pool is computed from total carbon input, lignin content and nitrogen fraction of the carbon input, using coefficients 0.85 and 0.018.
Annual CH4 emissions from rice are the sum over disaggregated sub-units of daily emission factor times cultivation period times harvested area.

n: Changes in carbon in cropland biomass (C_CCB) estimation approaches
s: C_CCB may be estimated by the gain-loss method (Chapter 2 Equation 2.7) or the stock-difference method (Chapter 2 Equation 2.8), with the stock-difference method restricted to Tier 2 or Tier 3.

n: Cropland perennial biomass loss estimate (L_max / L_mean)
s: Carbon losses from perennial cropland are estimated by multiplying the annual harvested or converted area by L_max or L_mean respectively.

n: Equation 5.0h steady-state C input to soil from crop residues
s: Equation 5.0h estimates annual C input from crop residues (above and below ground) plus manure and other organic amendments for the Tier 2 steady-state method.

n: Equation 5A.2.1 (NEW) Effect of controlling variables on CH4 flux from rice fields
s: A linear mixed model whose natural-log CH4 flux from rice fields is regressed on soil organic carbon, soil pH, pre-season water regime, growing-season water regime, climate type and organic amendment.

n: Equation 5A.2.2 (NEW) Default emission factor for continuously flooded rice fields
s: Derives a default CH4 emission factor for continuously flooded rice fields by evaluating the fitted model at reference conditions averaged over observations.

loc.section: 3 Developing of global and regional emission factors and scaling factors

n: Land use and management factor estimation with semi-parametric mixed effect model
s: Land use and management factors to 30 cm depth are estimated with a semi-parametric mixed effect model using covariates integrated over depth increments.

n: Lmax and Lmean calculation for agroforestry biomass
s: Table 5.1 states that L_max equals the biomass accumulation rate G times the harvest/maturity cycle, and L_mean equals L_max divided by 2.
SFo adjusts the emission factor for the type and amount of organic amendment applied, using an exponent of 0.59 on a sum of rate times conversion factor.

n: Paddy rice land-use factor (SOC stock change ratio)
s: The paddy rice land-use factor is the average of ratios of soil organic carbon between survey years for paired paddy rice and native vegetation comparisons.
Passive sub-pool SOC stock for year y is derived from the steady-state passive stock, previous-year passive stock and the passive pool decay rate k_p, with inflows from active and slow sub-pools.
Slow sub-pool fraction f_4 is computed as 1 minus f_5 minus (0.17 + 0.68·sand), with sand as the 0–30 cm sand fraction.

Monthly temperature effect on decomposition is computed from monthly average air temperature, optimum temperature and maximum temperature, and is set to 0 when monthly average temperature exceeds 45 °C.

s: Tier 1 estimates per-hectare biomass carbon stock change for each conversion type as carbon after conversion minus carbon before conversion plus one year of cropland growth, multiplied by annual converted area.

n: Tier 1 calculation steps for mineral soil SOC change in Cropland Remaining Cropland
s: The source gives a nine-step procedure for estimating SOC0, SOC(0-T) and annual mineral soil stock change for cropland remaining cropland using Table 5.6 factors and Equation 2.25.

n: Tier 1 mineral soil organic carbon stock change (Equation 2.25 reference)
s: Tier 1 estimates mineral soil organic C stock change as the difference between end and beginning SOC stocks divided by the time dependence D, with SOC from default reference stocks and stock change factors.

n: Tier 1 mineral soil SOC change calculation steps
s: Nine-step procedure computing initial and final SOC stocks and the average annual change in SOC for Land Converted to Cropland on mineral soils.

n: Tier 1 perennial woody cropland biomass change calculation
s: Tier 1 multiplies perennial woody cropland area by net biomass accumulation and subtracts losses from harvest or disturbance, with default assumptions on emission timing and accumulation period.

n: Tier 1 total CH4 emissions from rice cultivation
s: Annual CH4 emission for each rice ecosystem equals harvested area times adjusted daily emission factor times cultivation period, divided by 10^6 to give Gg.

n: Tier 2 steady-state SOC stock change calculation (Steps 5-8)
s: The source describes a multi-step procedure that computes passive, slow and active SOC sub-pool stocks and sums them into a total SOC stock change for Tier 2 steady-state inventories.

n: Tier 2 stock change factor approach for cropland mineral soils
s: Tier 2 derives country-specific stock change factors (F_LU, F_I, F_MG) relative to a reference SOC stock, with SOC_REF depth required to be the same for all land uses.

s: Worked example for forest converted to annual cropland on volcanic soil in tropical moist climate, giving SOC_0 of 58.0 t C/ha and an annual change of -0.6 t C/ha/yr.

n: Grassland management factors from grazing intensity meta-analysis
s: The source describes how updated default grassland management stock change factors were estimated from grazing intensity experiments using semi-parametric mixed effect models to a 30 cm depth.

n: Mineral soil stock change steps for Land Converted to Grassland
s: The source gives a stepwise procedure for estimating initial and final soil organic carbon stocks and the average annual change for mineral soils on land converted to grassland.

n: Tier 1 mineral soil organic C stock change (Equation 2.25)
s: Tier 1 estimates mineral soil organic C stock change from the difference between end and beginning SOC stocks divided by the time dependence of stock change factors.

n: Tier 1 SOC stock estimation with stock change factors
s: Tier 1 SOC stocks are estimated from default reference stocks multiplied by land-use, management and input stock change factors; the multiplicative form is not written out in the batch text.

n: Tier 2 country-specific stock change factor derivation
s: Tier 2 uses Equation 2.25 with country-specific stock change factors, reference stocks, climate regions, soil types and classification systems, with management and input factors derived against nominal grasslands.

n: Tier 3 dynamic model or measurement-based SOC approach
s: Tier 3 estimates annual soil C stock changes with dynamic models or measurement networks instead of simple stock change factors.

n: Worked example of grassland mineral soil C stock change (1 Mha tropical moist Ultisol)
s: The source gives a worked calculation of initial and final soil carbon stocks for 1 Mha of permanent grassland with SOC_REF of 47 t C/ha.

n: CO2 power-function decay model for reservoir flux
s: A power function of reservoir age gives annual CO2 flux, which is assumed to reach natural equilibrium at 100 years.
Downstream CH4 emissions are estimated by multiplying reservoir surface emissions by a fraction R_d.

n: Emission factor for Land converted to Flooded Land and Flooded Land remaining Flooded Land (Equations 7A.4 and 7A.5)
s: Emission factors integrate the diffusive CH4 model over reservoir age and add a bubbling term; the printed equations are not reliably recoverable from the extracted text.

n: Equation 7.10 reservoir surface and downstream CH4 emission terms
s: Reservoir surface CH4 is the double sum of area times emission factor times trophic adjustment, and Tier 1 downstream CH4 is surface CH4 times R_d.

n: Equation 7.10 total CH4 emissions from reservoirs older than 20 years
s: Total CH4 from reservoirs older than 20 years is the sum of surface emissions and downstream emissions.

n: Equation 7.11 trophic state adjustment from chlorophyll-a
s: The trophic state adjustment factor for a reservoir is 0.26 times its mean annual chlorophyll-a concentration, for use at Tier 2 and 3.

n: Equation 7.12 annual CH4 emission from other constructed waterbodies
s: Annual CH4 from ponds, ditches and other constructed waterbodies is the triple sum of area times emission factor times trophic adjustment.

n: Equation 7.13 annual CO2 emissions from reservoirs up to 20 years old
s: Total annual CO2-C emission from land converted to flooded land is the sum over climate zones and reservoirs of area times the emission factor for reservoirs up to 20 years old.

n: Equation 7.14 emission factor for CO2 from reservoirs by soil type
s: The Tier 2 CO2 emission factor for a reservoir in a climate zone is the sum over soil types of the soil area fraction times the soil organic carbon stock times a climate-zone scaling factor.

n: Equation 7.15(B) surface CH4 emission from reservoirs ≤20 years old
s: Reservoir surface CH4 emission is the double sum over climate zones and reservoirs of EF times total area.

n: Equation 7.15(C) downstream CH4 emission from reservoirs ≤20 years old
s: Downstream CH4 emission is the surface-emission sum multiplied by the downstream ratio R_d, with a Tier 1 simplification to F_res × R_d.

n: Equation 7.15 total annual CH4 emissions from reservoirs ≤20 years old
s: Total annual CH4 emission from all reservoirs ≤20 years old is the sum of reservoir surface emissions and downstream emissions.

n: Equation 7.16 indicative anthropogenic CH4 emissions for flooded land remaining flooded land (>20 years)
s: Indicative anthropogenic CH4 emission for reservoirs older than 20 years sums area-weighted EF_age>20 values excluding unmanaged waterbodies, plus downstream emissions.

n: Equation 7.17 indicative anthropogenic CO2 emissions in land converted to flooded land
s: Indicative anthropogenic CO2 emission for reservoirs ≤20 years old sums area times EF_CO2 over climate zones and reservoirs, excluding unmanaged lakes, rivers and wetlands.

n: Equation 7.18 indicative anthropogenic CH4 emissions in land converted to flooded land (≤20 years)
s: Indicative anthropogenic CH4 emission for reservoirs ≤20 years old sums area-weighted EF_age≤20 values excluding unmanaged lakes, rivers and wetlands, plus downstream emissions.
Log10 of diffusive CH4 emission is modelled as a linear function of reservoir age, a temperature factor and the log10 of littoral area percentage.
Log10 of ebullitive CH4 emission is modelled as a linear function of solar irradiance Q_rad and the log10 of littoral area percentage.
Log10 of diffusive CO2 emission is modelled as a linear function of temperature factor, log10 reservoir age, soil organic carbon and log10 reservoir area.

n: Log-transformed mean emission factor for constructed waterbodies
s: Mean CH4 emission factors for small constructed waterbodies are computed on log-transformed data, after annualizing per-study mean fluxes.

n: R_D multiplier (downstream to reservoir-surface CH4 ratio)

n: Land converted to settlements biomass change (Tier 1 and Tier 2)
s: Biomass change on land converted to settlements is estimated from the area converted multiplied by the difference between biomass before conversion (B_Before) and after conversion (B_After), with Tier 1 setting B_After to zero.

n: Settlements Tier 1 step-by-step biomass change method
s: Tier 1 estimates CO2 from land converted to settlements by applying Equation 2.16 per land-use type with default B_before and B_after set to zero, summing and multiplying by 44/12.

n: Settlements Tier 2 land-use conversion matrix method

n: Urban tree biomass removal factor CRW (Tier 2A)
s: Tier 2A estimates urban tree biomass change as annual carbon accumulation per hectare of tree crown cover using the default CRW values in Table 8.1.

n: 2006 IPCC MCF Arrhenius model for liquid/slurry
s: The 2006 IPCC Guidelines set liquid/slurry MCF equal to f, where f is computed from an Arrhenius-type temperature function.

n: Annual N excretion, Tier 2 Option 1 (intake minus retained fraction)

n: Annual N excretion, Tier 2 Option 2 (intake minus retention)

n: Approximate emission factor for livestock without species methods
s: Approximate factors scale a Tier 1 factor of a similar digestive-system animal by weight ratio to the 0.75 power.

n: Daily N intake from dry matter intake and crude protein (Equation 10.32A)

n: Daily N retention for breeding sows (Equation 10.33A)
s: Annual N retention for breeding sows is the sum of N gained by the sow and N in weaned piglets.

n: Daily N retention for growing pigs (Equation 10.33C)
s: Growing-pig N retention sums over growth stages the weight gain times the stage N gain fraction, then divides by the production period.

n: Daily N retention for layer hens and pullets or broilers (Equations 10.33D and 10.33E)
s: Hen N retention combines live-weight N content times daily weight gain with egg N content times egg mass; pullets and broilers use weight gain over the production period.

n: Digester methane balance and leakage rate (Equations 10A.5 and 10A.6)
s: Defines the digester methane balance and the leakage methane as the digester leakage rate times the methane produced.

n: DMI for lactating dairy cows (simplified Tier 2)

n: Enteric fermentation CH4 emissions from a livestock category (Tier 1)

n: Manure management CH4 emission calculation procedure (Tier 1, Tier 1a, Tier 2)
s: Six-step procedure for estimating CH4 from manure management using volatile solid excretion, manure management system fractions, and emission factors or MCF and B0, summed across categories.

n: Manure methane model f equation (temperature-dependent methane conversion factor)
s: The model computes a temperature-dependent f parameter with the van't Hoff-Arrhenius equation from T1, T2, Ea and R, where T2 is the monthly manure temperature in Kelvin.

n: Manure VS methane production calculation sequence (monthly model)
s: The monthly model tracks VS loaded, emptying, available VS, VS consumed and CH4 volume over three years.

n: MCF calculation from monthly manure model (Annex 10A.2 example)
s: The source states that the methane conversion factor (MCF) is calculated in the Results section using the third-year model outputs.
Computes the effective methane conversion factor for the combination of digester and digestate storage from residual gas share, digester leakage rate and digestate storage MCF.
N_gain is the fraction of nitrogen retained per kg of body weight gain over the production period, with a default of 0.028.

n: N2 fraction lost as N2 from manure management (Frac_N2_MS)
s: Frac_N2_MS is estimated as the N2:N2O ratio times EF3, with a default ratio of 3.

n: 直接N2O排放（粪便管理）公式 Equation 10.25
s: Direct N2O emissions from manure management are the sum over systems of (N excretion times AWMS, plus co-digestate N) times EF3 times 44/28.

n: 间接N2O（淋溶与径流）公式 Equation 10.27 and 10.29
s: Nitrogen lost by leaching and runoff from manure management is estimated from managed manure N times Frac_LeachMS, then converted to indirect N2O with EF_5 and 44/28.

n: 间接N2O（NH3与NOx挥发）公式 Equation 10.26 and 10.28
s: Nitrogen lost by volatilisation of NH3 and NOx is estimated from managed manure N times Frac_GasMS, then converted to indirect N2O with EF_4 and 44/28.
Pregnancy net energy is the maintenance net energy multiplied by a pregnancy coefficient.

n: NE_wool net energy to produce wool
s: Net energy for wool is estimated from annual wool production and an energy value per kilogram of wool.
Net energy for draft work is estimated as a fraction of daily maintenance energy per hour of work.
Dietary net energy for maintenance can be estimated from REM, default energy density, and DE percent.

n: Net energy for activity (NEa), cattle and buffalo, Equation 10.4
s: Activity energy for cattle and buffalo is the product of a feeding-situation coefficient and maintenance energy.

n: Net energy for activity (NEa), sheep and goats, Equation 10.5
s: Activity energy for sheep and goats is the product of a feeding-situation coefficient and live weight.

n: Net energy for growth (NEg), cattle and buffalo, Equation 10.6
s: Growth energy for cattle and buffalo is estimated from average body weight, daily weight gain and mature weight with a sex-specific coefficient C.

n: Net energy for growth (NEg), sheep and goats, Equation 10.7
s: Growth energy for sheep and goats is annual weight gain per lamb or kid times a constant-based term divided by 365.

n: Net energy for lactation for sheep and goats, milk known (Equation 10.9)
s: For sheep and goats with known milk output, lactation energy is milk production times energy per kg of milk.

n: Net energy for lactation for sheep and goats, milk unknown (Equation 10.10)
s: When milk output is unknown for sheep, lactation energy is estimated from lamb weight gain to weaning, with milk yield taken as about five times that gain.

n: Net energy for lactation (NEl), cattle, buffalo and dairy, Equation 10.8
s: Lactation energy for cattle and buffalo is milk output multiplied by a term in milk fat content.
Net energy for maintenance is computed as Cf_i multiplied by live weight raised to the power 0.75.

n: Nitrogen flow pathway for manure N2O and NH3/NOx emissions (Figure 10.5)
s: Figure 10.5 maps manure N flows from excretion (Nex) through storage (NMS), application (NAM) and grazing deposition (NPRP) to volatilisation, direct N2O, indirect N2O and leaching losses, with the equation and EF/Frac symbol attached to each flow.
Combines a prestorage MCF with the digester plus digestate storage MCF to give the MCF for the full chain.

n: Proposed 2019 monthly-temperature MCF model for liquid/slurry
s: The 2019 Refinement proposes computing liquid/slurry MCF with monthly temperatures in each IPCC climate region for selected retention times using a spreadsheet model.

n: REG ratio of net energy for growth to digestible energy
s: REG is a regression function of digestibility used for net energy for growth including wool growth.

n: REM ratio of net energy for maintenance to digestible energy
s: REM is a regression function of digestibility used for cattle, buffalo, sheep and goats.

n: Sheep and goat C_pregnancy from birth fractions
s: When birth-type data are missing, the sheep and goat pregnancy coefficient is computed from the lamb-to-pregnant-ewe ratio.

n: Simplified Tier 2 enteric methane emission factor (Equation 10.21a)
s: Simplified Tier 2 formula that computes an annual enteric methane emission factor from dry matter intake and methane yield.
An Excel model computes a country or regional Methane Conversion Factor from monthly temperatures, manure removal months and constants, following three sections (inputs, model calculations, results).

n: Tier 1 method for enteric fermentation methane
s: The Tier 1 method estimates enteric fermentation methane from readily available animal population data multiplied by default emission factors per population subgroup.

loc.section: Tier 1 Approach for methane emissions from Enteric Fermentation

n: Tier 1a advanced Tier 1 method for enteric fermentation
s: Tier 1a splits populations into high and low productivity systems and applies default emission factors per productivity system.

n: Tier 2 CH4 emission factor from manure management (Equation 10.23)
s: The annual CH4 emission factor per animal equals VS daily excretion times 365, times B0, times 0.67, times the sum of MCF weighted by AWMS fractions divided by 100.
Energy-balance Tier 2 formula that computes an annual enteric methane emission factor per animal category from gross energy intake and the methane conversion factor.

n: Tier 2 method for enteric fermentation methane
s: The Tier 2 method derives category-specific emission factors from gross energy intake and methane conversion factor Ym instead of using defaults.

n: Total emissions from livestock enteric fermentation (Tier 1)
s: The source lists a Tier 1 equation for total enteric fermentation emissions, but the formula is not present in this batch.

n: Total N2O emissions for animal type T (Equations 10A.10 to 10A.27 set)

n: Total N2O emissions from manure management for animal type T
s: The source indexes equations for total N2O emissions for animal type T from manure management, but the formulas are not present in this batch.

s: Daily volatile solid excretion is estimated from gross energy intake, digestibility, urinary energy fraction and ash content.

n: Above-ground residue dry matter alternative estimation (Table 11.2)
s: Above-ground residue dry matter is estimated as crop yield times a slope plus an intercept, using crop-specific or default parameters.

n: Activity data parameters for indirect N2O emissions (F_SN, F_ON, F_PRP, F_CR, F_SOM)
s: Indirect N2O estimation requires annual N input terms for synthetic fertiliser, organic fertiliser, grazing urine and dung, crop residue and mineralised soil organic C, each taken from the direct-emission activity data section.

n: EF from N addition experiments at non-agricultural sites (review-based)

n: EF from N2O emission and N deposition measurements at non-agricultural sites
s: Where N2O and N deposition are measured together, EF is N2O divided by N deposition, which may double count N2O from mineralisation.

s: Tier 1 direct N2O emission from managed soils is estimated as the sum of N2O-N from N inputs, organic soils and urine/dung deposited on pasture.

n: F_AM (animal manure N applied to soils)
s: F_AM is managed manure N available for soil application after subtracting manure used for feed, fuel or construction, with fallback to N_MMS_Avb if those fractions are unavailable.

n: F_CR (N in crop residues and forage/pasture renewal)
s: F_CR sums above-ground and below-ground crop residue N returned to soils by crop type, adjusting for removal and burning, and includes N from forage or pasture renewal.
F_ON is the total annual organic N applied to soils other than by grazing animals, summed from manure, sewage, compost and other organic amendments.

n: F_PRP (urine and dung N deposited by grazing animals)
s: F_PRP sums animal number times N excretion times the fraction deposited on pasture, range and paddock over all livestock categories.
The default Frac_GASM is the sum of the arithmetic mean NH3 EF and the arithmetic mean NOx EF from manure and excreta.

n: Indirect soil N2O emission factors EF4 and EF5 (Tier 1 default)
s: The method for indirect N2O emissions uses EF_4 for volatilised and re-deposited N and EF_5 for N lost through leaching/runoff.

n: Mineralised N from soil organic C loss (F_SOM)
s: Net annual N mineralised from mineral soil organic C loss is calculated from the average annual soil C loss using Equation 11.8, with the exact operator form recoverable only approximately from the garbled source text.

n: N2O from atmospheric deposition of volatilised N (Tier 1, Equation 11.9)
s: Indirect N2O from atmospheric deposition of volatilised N is calculated from synthetic fertiliser N and organic N/urine-dung N times volatilisation fractions and EF4, then converted to N2O by multiplying by 44/28.

n: N2O from atmospheric deposition, Tier 2 disaggregated form (Equation 11.11)
s: Tier 2 expands the atmospheric deposition equation to sum synthetic fertiliser N across different conditions i, each with its own volatilisation fraction, as an illustrative modification.

n: N2O from N leaching and runoff (Tier 1, Equation 11.10)
s: Indirect N2O from leaching and runoff is calculated from total N inputs (synthetic, organic, urine/dung, crop residue, SOM mineralisation) times Frac_LEACH-(H) and EF5, then converted to N2O by multiplying by 44/28.
Reported N2O mass is obtained from N2O-N by multiplying by 44/28.

n: Tier 1 aggregated NH3 + NOx EF for synthetic fertiliser
s: The Tier 1 aggregated NH3 + NOx emission factor for synthetic fertiliser is the arithmetic mean of default EFs for individual fertiliser types, weighted by 2007-2015 IFA use.

n: Combined method for remaining material-use HWP fraction
s: Where direct inventories cover specific end uses, the remaining fraction of the three default commodities is estimated with a flux data method such as Equation 12.2.

n: Cross-check of HWP domestic production against wood supply
s: Activity data validation by checking that domestic HWP production balances with available wood supply, plus trade unit values and per capita apparent consumption.

n: Equation 12.10 carbon inflow allocated to land use categories
s: Carbon inflow into a semi-finished HWP commodity class is allocated to a land use category using the share of harvest from that category in total harvest.

n: Equation 12.11 carbon in traded HWP feedstock serving as wood fuel and raw material
s: Carbon in traded HWP feedstock commodity class j is computed from the traded quantity and the carbon conversion factor cf_j.

Under the atmospheric-flow approach, annual CO2 fluxes combine the stock-change term for HWP in use with net trade terms for wood fuel and feedstock; exact notation is not legible in the extraction.

Under the production approach, Equation 12.7 gives carbon inflow for a semi-finished HWP class from domestic-harvest production; the explicit formula is not legible.

s: Carbon stock in each HWP class and its annual change follow a first-order decay function with decay constant k derived from half-life.
The half-life of an HWP commodity class in use is the adjusted ESL multiplied by ln(2).

s: Annual CO2 emissions and removals from the HWP pool in use are the sum of net carbon stock changes across the selected HWP classes, converted by 44/12.

n: DOC in sludge from carbon content and volatile suspended solids fraction
s: In this refinement, sludge DOC is estimated as the product of carbon content and the volatile suspended solids fraction, applicable mainly to industrial sludge with evenly distributed carbon.

n: First Order Decay (FOD) model for SWDS CH4 emissions
s: The FOD method estimates CH4 emissions from SWDS using waste generation rate and waste composition as key parameters; the formula itself is not given in this excerpt.

n: Waste stream analysis for activity data
s: A more accurate but data-intensive approach follows waste streams from generation through treatment to disposal, tracking changes in mass, moisture and DOCm.

s: Annual CH4 emissions from solid waste disposal are summed over waste categories as CH4 generated minus recovered CH4, times (1 minus oxidation factor).
CH4 generated in year T equals DDOCm decomposed in year T times the CH4 volume fraction times 16/12.

n: CH4 emission from gas collection system by flow rate and concentration
s: CH4 emission from the gas collection system is the product of CH4 content and landfill gas flow rate from the pipe, with flow estimated from gas velocity and pipe area.

n: CH4 recovery estimation by number of SWDS with landfill gas recovery
s: When CH4 recovery is estimated from the number of SWDS with landfill gas recovery, a default recovery efficiency of 20 percent is suggested.

n: CH4 recovery estimation by total capacity of utilisation equipment or flares
s: When CH4 recovery is based on total capacity of utilisation equipment or flares sold, a conservative approach is to estimate total recovery as 35 percent of installed capacity.

n: CH4 surface emission from flux density and zone area with conservativeness factor
s: Surface CH4 emission is estimated per zone as average flux density times zone area, then multiplied by a conservativeness factor of 1.37 as proposed by the CDM Executive Board.

s: The accumulated DDOCm at year end T equals deposits in year T plus the previous accumulation after first-order decay, and the decomposed amount is the previous accumulation times (1 − e^−k).

n: Decomposable DOC from waste disposal data (Equation 3.2)
s: The mass of decomposable DOC deposited is the product of waste mass, degradable organic carbon fraction, decomposable fraction and MCF.
Degradable organic carbon in bulk waste is estimated as a weighted sum of degradable carbon fractions of waste types using default carbon content values.

n: Half-life and methane generation rate relationship
s: The FOD reaction constant k equals ln(2) divided by the half-life of DOCm.

n: MCF for managed SWDS with active aeration (measured CH4 and CO2 fractions)
s: MCF for SWDS under active aeration is defined from measured CH4 and CO2 fractions in landfill gas before and during aeration, but the equation body is not reliably recoverable from this extraction.
CH4 generation potential equals DDOCm times CH4 fraction in landfill gas times the 16/12 CH4/C molecular weight ratio.

n: CH4 emission factor for open burning of waste
s: The default CH4 emission factor for open burning of waste is 6500 g per tonne of MSW wet weight, unless a more appropriate factor applies.

n: CH4 emission factors for MSW incineration by technology and operation mode
s: Table 5.3 gives Japanese CH4 emission factors for MSW incineration by operation mode and furnace technology, in kg per Gg waste on a wet weight basis.

n: CH4 emission factors for pyrolysis-melting and gasification-melting plants of MSW
s: Table 5.3a gives commercial-scale CH4 emission factors for MSW pyrolysis-melting and gasification-melting plants by reactor type.

n: CO2 emission from incineration and open burning of waste (oxidation factor and carbon parameters)
s: Table 5.2 (Updated) gives default parameter values for CO2 emission factors from waste incineration and open burning, with several entries deferred to Notes for MSW.

n: Combined pyrolysis or gasification and melting system process description
s: In the combined system, MSW is thermally decomposed in a pyrolysis or gasification reactor, and primary gas and char are oxidised in a melting furnace to produce secondary gas that is cleaned and emitted from the stack.

n: Consecutive approach for CO2 from waste incineration and open burning
s: The source describes a consecutive approach: identify waste types, compile waste amounts, apply default dry matter, carbon and fossil carbon factors, calculate CO2 and report in Annex 1 worksheets.

n: N2O emission factors for MSW incineration by country and technology
s: Table 5.4 lists example N2O emission factors for MSW incineration by country and furnace technology, in g N2O per tonne MSW incinerated on wet weight basis.

n: N2O emission factors for pyrolysis-melting and gasification-melting plants of MSW
s: Table 5.4A gives commercial-scale N2O emission factors for MSW pyrolysis-melting and gasification-melting plants by reactor type.

n: CH4 emission factor EF_j = B_o × MCF_j

s: Computes the pathway emission factor as the maximum CH4 producing capacity times the methane correction factor for that pathway.

n: CH4 emissions from domestic wastewater per treatment/discharge pathway (Equation 6.1)
s: Estimates CH4 emissions for each domestic wastewater treatment or discharge pathway as the organics minus sludge removed, multiplied by the emission factor, minus recovered CH4.

n: Default MCF for aerobic centralised domestic wastewater treatment plants
s: The aerobic treatment MCF is 0.03 from 14 accepted full-scale plants, with standard deviation 0.024 and range 0.003–0.09.

n: Equation 6.7 (updated) N2O emissions from domestic wastewater effluent
s: Estimates N2O from domestic wastewater effluent discharged to aquatic environments as effluent nitrogen times EF_EFFLUENT times 44.
